lessons.title: Introduction and Excellence of the Holy Quran
lessons.notes_html:
This is a textbook lesson of the book. There is no written exercise for it in the book; these notes give the facts printed in the book's own lesson.

Introduction to the Holy Quran

The literal meaning of the word "Quran" is: to read, and one of its meanings is also "a book that is read". Its terminological meaning is: the Word of Allah Almighty which was revealed to Hazrat Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, the Seal of the Prophets (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions) through Hazrat Jibreel (peace be upon him) and was written in the Mushafs (bound copies).

  • The Holy Quran has 30 Paras, 114 Surahs, 558 Ruku and 6236 Ayats.
  • The first Surah is "Al-Fatiha" and the last Surah is "An-Nas".
  • The largest Surah is "Al-Baqarah" and the smallest Surah is "Al-Kawthar".
  • The great Ayat that describes the greatness and majesty of Allah Almighty is "Ayat-ul-Kursi".
  • Every Surah consists of at least three Ayats, and every Surah has a special content and subject.
  • Except for Surah At-Tawbah, Bismillah-ir-Rahman-ir-Raheem is written at the beginning of every Surah.
  • The literal meaning of "Ayat" is: a sign or mark. In terminology, a part of the Holy Quran is called an Ayat, and at the end of that part there is a sign of a circle.

Names of the Holy Quran

The real name of the Holy Quran is "Al-Quran" itself, but the scholars have counted many other names besides it, some of the famous names among which are:

  • Al-Quran: This is the original and personal name of the Holy Word.
  • Al-Furqan: The book that distinguishes between truth and falsehood.
  • Az-Zikr: The book of advice.
  • Al-Kitab: Specifically the Book of Allah Almighty, that is, the Holy Quran.
  • Al-Huda: The book that shows the way.
  • An-Noor: The book of light.
  • Al-Haqq: The established book.
  • Ash-Shifa: The book that removes physical and spiritual diseases.
  • At-Tanzeel: The revealed book.

Revelation of the Quran

The Holy Quran is the eternal and everlasting Word of Allah Almighty, which is present in the "Lawh-e-Mahfooz". As Allah Almighty has said: BAL HUWA QUR-ANUN MAJEED, FEE LAWHIN MAHFOOZ (Surah Al-Buruj: 22) - Translation: (This is no ordinary book) rather this Quran is a glorious book, kept in the Lawh-e-Mahfooz.

The Holy Quran reached the earth from the Lawh-e-Mahfooz in two stages:

  • First stage: The whole Holy Quran was revealed all at once to "Bayt-ul-Izzah" on the sky of the world. As it is in Surah Al-Qadr: INNA ANZALNAHU FEE LAYLATIL-QADR (Al-Qadr: 1) - Translation: We sent down this Quran in the Night of Qadr.
  • Second stage: After that, according to need and occasion, from time to time, Hazrat Jibreel (peace be upon him), by the command of Allah Almighty, kept bringing it down to Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) in the form of different Ayats and Surahs. This revelation was completed gradually in twenty-two years and some months, of which twelve years and some months were revealed in Makkah Mukarramah before the Hijrah, and the rest in Madinah Munawwarah, the place of migration.

Gradual Revelation and Its Wisdoms

The second stage of the revelation of the Holy Quran is called gradual (stage-by-stage) revelation. The command of Allah Almighty is: WA QUR-ANAN FARAQNAHU LITAQRA-AHU ALAN-NASI ALA MUKTHIN WA NAZZALNAHU TANZEELA (Al-Isra: 106) - We sent down the Holy Quran little by little so that you may recite it to the people slowly, and We sent it down gradually. The wisdoms of gradual revelation are:

  • Memorising the Holy Quran became easy.
  • Human natures were gradually prepared to act upon the different kinds of commands present in the Holy Quran; if all the commands had been revealed all at once, leaving old habits and acting upon the new commands would have become very difficult.
  • When the troubles and torments of the opponents exceeded the limit and then some revelation was sent down, it became a cause of relief and comfort for the hearts of the Muslims.
  • By giving a timely answer when people asked questions at different times, the truthfulness of the Holy Quran was proved.

Lawh-e-Mahfooz: By it is meant that tablet or book which is safe from every kind of change and is the origin of all the commands, orders and words of Allah.

Bayt-ul-Izzah: This is the place on the sky of the world where the whole Holy Quran was brought down all at once from the Lawh-e-Mahfooz, then from there it was revealed little by little to the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him).

Makki and Madani Surahs

With regard to revelation, the Surahs of the Holy Quran have been divided into two parts: the Ayats or Surahs which were revealed before the Hijrah to Madinah Munawwarah are called Makki, and those which were revealed after the Hijrah to Madinah are called Madani. In this regard, the number of Makki Surahs is 86 and the number of Madani Surahs is 28. On the basis of their basic characteristics, Makki and Madani Surahs can be recognised:

  • Makki Surahs are generally short, and in them mostly Tawheed, Prophethood, summary commands about the Hereafter, religion, worship, and the events of the previous nations and the stories of the Prophets (peace be upon them) have been described; whereas Madani Surahs are long, and in them there are mostly detailed commands of the Shariah.
  • In the Surahs and Ayats of the Makki period, the people of faith were told their duties and the misguided people were warned of the end of the past nations; whereas in the Madani Surahs and Ayats detailed commands were told, such as Zakat, Jihad and the issues of fighting and the punishments for sins, etc., and together with them basic guidance was given about the commands of different issues of life, of social, economic and family nature.
  • In Makki Surahs, along with the believers, mostly the polytheists have been addressed and made to understand; whereas in Madani Surahs, along with the Muslims, mention of the hypocrites and the People of the Book is also found.
  • Mostly in Makki Surahs the address is with the words "YA AYYUHAN-NAS" (O mankind!), and in Madani Surahs the address is with the words "YA AYYUHAL-LAZEENA AAMANU" (O believers!).

Greatness and Excellence of the Holy Quran

The Holy Quran is the last book sent down by Allah Almighty. Just as the Being of Allah Almighty is of greatness and glory and is free from every defect and fault, in the same way His Book is also of greatness and high glory, which is free from every kind of mistake and deficiency.

  • The command of Allah Almighty is: INNA NAHNU NAZZALNAZ-ZIKRA WA INNA LAHU LA-HAFIZOON (Al-Hijr: 9) - Translation: Indeed, We alone have sent down this book of advice, and surely We alone are its guardians.
  • There is a great effect in this Book: LAW ANZALNA HAZAL-QUR-ANA ALA JABALIN LARA-AYTAHU KHASHI-AN MUTASADDI-AN MIN KHASHYATILLAH (Al-Hashr: 21) - Translation: If We had sent down this Quran on a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and split from the fear of Allah Almighty; and these examples We state for the people so that they may reflect.
  • The Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) said: KHAYRUKUM MAN TA-ALLAMAL-QUR-ANA WA AL-LAMAHU (Sahih Bukhari, Hadith: 5027) - Translation: The best person among you is the one who learns the Quran and teaches it.
  • The Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) said that I am leaving among you two such things that after acting upon them you will never go astray: one of them is the Quran and the other is my Sunnah; both of them will never separate, until both of them arrive to me at the Hawd-e-Kawthar. (Mustadrak Hakim, Hadith: 4321)

Qualities of the Holy Quran

  • (1) Being a revealed book: The Holy Quran is the last revealed book of Allah Almighty, which is the last message for the guidance of man. It is a code of action for the nations of the whole world and a guarantor of success in this world and the Hereafter. There is no equal to this great blessing of Allah Almighty. Reading it and listening to it is a cause of blessing and reward; understanding it and reflecting on its smallest matters is a cause of guidance and success in both worlds.
  • (2) Being revealed in the Arabic language: INNA ANZALNAHU QUR-ANAN ARABIYYAN LA-ALLAKUM TA-QILOON (Surah Yusuf: 2) - Translation: We have sent down this Quran in the Arabic language so that you may understand. That is the reason why the Holy Quran has been read for centuries in the same way as it was read at the time of its revelation.
  • (3) Uniqueness of style: The greatest excellence of the Holy Quran is that it is the Word of Allah Almighty; it is alone and separate in its style and manner and is a book that dwells in the soul. There is no contradiction or difference in its contents and subjects: AFALA YATADABBAROONAL-QUR-AN, WA LAW KANA MIN INDI GHAYRILLAHI LAWJADOO FEEHI IKHTILAFAN KATHEERA (An-Nisa: 82). It is in a Hadith that the excellence of the Holy Quran over other speech is just as Allah Almighty has excellence over all creation. (Shuab-ul-Iman by Bayhaqi: 2208)
  • (4) A book free from doubt and suspicion: The Holy Quran has announced its greatness right at the beginning: ZALIKAL-KITABU LA RAYBA FEEHI HUDAN LIL-MUTTAQEEN (Surah Al-Baqarah: 2) - This is the Book in which there is no room for any doubt that it is the Word of Allah Almighty; it is a guide for the God-fearing.

The Holy Quran: A Way of Life

Until the Day of Judgment, the Holy Quran is a complete code of life for all the material, spiritual, religious and worldly needs of the whole universe, which is an everlasting and universal law. The Holy Quran guides us in all fields of life: together with the issues of the reality of human life, halal and haram, good and evil, piety and worship, it also guides in issues such as Shariah commands and advice, government and trade, war and peace, and tells social, economic, political and moral teachings and principles to make character better and better.

Rights and Etiquette of the Holy Quran

The Holy Quran is a blessed book; its glory is greater than other ordinary books, therefore its rights and etiquette become obligatory on the Muslims:

  • (1) To believe in the Holy Quran.
  • (2) To read the Holy Quran in a state of wudu and to listen to it attentively.
  • (3) To understand the Holy Quran, and to ponder and reflect in it.
  • (4) To act upon the Holy Quran.
  • (5) To spread the teaching of the Holy Quran.
  • (6) To implement the system of the Holy Quran individually and collectively.

Therefore we should try to live our lives well according to the commands of the Holy Quran and fully act upon its teachings.

lessons.title: Translation and Explanation of Selected Verses
lessons.notes_html:
Selected Verses - Translations

Verse about fearing for weak offspring: وَلْيَخْشَ الَّذِينَ لَوْ تَرَكُوا مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّةً ضِعَافًا خَافُوا عَلَيْهِمْ فَلْيَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَلْيَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا

  • Translation: And those (who fear Allah Almighty) should fear - those who, if they left weak offspring behind them, would fear for their (ruin) - so they should fear Allah and speak straightforward words.

Verse about the wealth of orphans: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوَالَ الْيَتَامَى ظُلْمًا إِنَّمَا يَأْكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ نَارًا وَسَيَصْلَوْنَ سَعِيرًا

  • Translation: Indeed, those who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly only consume fire in their bellies, and they will enter a blazing Fire.

Verse about handing over the orphans' wealth: وَآتُوا الْيَتَامَى أَمْوَالَهُمْ وَلَا تَتَبَدَّلُوا الْخَبِيثَ بِالطَّيِّبِ وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَهُمْ إِلَى أَمْوَالِكُمْ إِنَّهُ كَانَ حُوبًا كَبِيرًا

  • Translation: And hand over to the orphans the wealth that is under your care, and do not exchange their pure and fine wealth for your defective and bad wealth, nor consume their wealth by mixing it with your own wealth, for that is a very great sin.

Verse about women's dower: وَآتُوا النِّسَاءَ صَدُقَاتِهِنَّ نِحْلَةً فَإِنْ طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَنْ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ نَفْسًا فَكُلُوهُ هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا

  • Translation: And give women their dower (mahr) happily. Yes, if they willingly give up a part of it for you, then consume it with pleasure and delight.

Verse about trade and not killing yourselves: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِالْبَاطِلِ إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ تِجَارَةً عَنْ تَرَاضٍ مِنْكُمْ وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِكُمْ رَحِيمًا

  • Translation: O believers! Do not consume one another's wealth unjustly among yourselves, except when (the transaction) is trade with your mutual consent (then there is no harm); and do not kill yourselves. Indeed, Allah Almighty is Merciful to you.

Verse about worship and doing good: وَاعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَلَا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئًا وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا وَبِذِي الْقُرْبَى وَالْيَتَامَى وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَالْجَارِ ذِي الْقُرْبَى وَالْجَارِ الْجُنُبِ وَالصَّاحِبِ بِالْجَنْبِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ وَمَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ مَنْ كَانَ مُخْتَالًا فَخُورًا

  • Translation: And worship Allah alone, and do not associate anyone with Him; and do good to parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, the neighbouring relative, the distant neighbour, the companion by your side, the traveller, and those under your authority. Indeed, Allah does not love the arrogant and boastful (nor those who are miserly).

Verse prescribed for the Children of Israel about killing: مِنْ أَجْلِ ذَلِكَ كَتَبْنَا عَلَى بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ أَنَّهُ مَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْسًا بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ فَسَادٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ النَّاسَ جَمِيعًا وَمَنْ أَحْيَاهَا فَكَأَنَّمَا أَحْيَا النَّاسَ جَمِيعًا وَلَقَدْ جَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُنَا بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ ثُمَّ إِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنْهُمْ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فِي الْأَرْضِ لَمُسْرِفُونَ

  • Translation: For this reason We prescribed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a person without (retribution for) a life or (punishment for) corruption in the land, it is as if he killed all mankind; and whoever saves a life, it is as if he saved all mankind. And indeed Our Messengers came to them with clear signs, yet many of them even after that are transgressors in the land.

Verse about the Messenger sent with guidance: هُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ بِالْهُدَى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْمُشْرِكُونَ

  • Translation: He (Allah Almighty) is the One who sent His Messenger with guidance and the true religion, so that He may make it prevail over all religions, even though the polytheists dislike it.

Verse about permission to fight: أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقَاتَلُونَ بِأَنَّهُمْ ظُلِمُوا وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى نَصْرِهِمْ لَقَدِيرٌ

  • Translation: Permission (to fight) has been given to those against whom the disbelievers wage war, because they have been wronged; and indeed Allah is Able to help them.

Verse about those given power in the land: الَّذِينَ إِنْ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَقَامُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتَوُا الزَّكَاةَ وَأَمَرُوا بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَنَهَوْا عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَلِلَّهِ عَاقِبَةُ الْأُمُورِ

  • Translation: Those who, if We give them power in the land, establish Salah, give Zakat, enjoin good and forbid evil; and with Allah is the end of all matters.

Rights of the Orphan - Verse 6 of Surah An-Nisa

  • The orphan should be tested, and when he reaches the age of marriage and maturity (rushd) in managing wealth is seen in him, his wealth should be handed over to him.
  • The orphan's wealth should not be wasted in extravagance (israf), nor consumed hastily out of fear that the orphan will grow up.
  • A guardian who is rich should refrain from (consuming) the orphan's wealth, and one who is poor may consume according to custom.
  • When the orphan's wealth is handed over to him, witnesses should be appointed, and Allah Almighty is sufficient as One who takes account.

Meanings of Buloogh and Rushd, and the Method of Handing Over Wealth

  • Buloogh means reaching the age of marriage. Rushd means possessing sound judgment in managing wealth and business.
  • The Holy Quran states: keep testing the orphans until, when they reach the age of marriage, if you then see any sound judgment in them, hand over their wealth to them; and when you hand over their wealth to them, appoint witnesses over them.
  • Why protection of the orphan's wealth is necessary: because it is the means of their livelihood and upbringing (Allah Almighty made it the cause of their sustenance); being minor and immature, orphans cannot protect it themselves; even a little negligence can harm both the wealth and its owner; and dishonesty in it is a very great sin.

Responsibilities of the Guardian of the Orphan

  • Protect the orphan's wealth and do not commit dishonesty in it.
  • Do not hand over wealth to an immature and minor orphan; instead arrange for his basic needs (food, clothing, education and upbringing). Guardians are also told: do not hand over wealth to an immature and minor orphan, but from his wealth arrange for his needs and speak good words to him.
  • Test the orphan, and when he becomes adult and sound in judgment, hand over his wealth to him in the presence of witnesses.
  • A rich guardian should refrain from the orphan's wealth, and a poor guardian may consume only according to custom.
  • Hand over to the orphan the wealth that is under your care; do not exchange their pure and fine wealth for your defective and bad wealth, and do not consume their wealth by mixing it with your own wealth - that is a very great sin.

Punishment for Dishonesty in the Orphan's Wealth

  • Those who consume the orphan's wealth unjustly only consume fire in their bellies and will enter a blazing Fire.
  • In Hadith too, consuming the orphan's wealth has been counted among the major sins. (Sahih Bukhari, Kitab-ul-Muharibeen, Hadith: 6857)

Wealth, Killing and Human Life

  • "Do not kill yourselves" means that in Islam unjust killing is forbidden - neither kill any other human being unjustly, nor kill yourself (suicide). Three things of every human being are of the greatest importance: his life, wealth and honour; Islam guarantees these three things to its followers. Indeed, Allah Almighty is Merciful to you.
  • Unlawful ways of acquiring wealth: consuming wealth by unjust and unlawful means is forbidden. Things that are themselves forbidden, for example pork, wine and intoxicants - their trade and use is already unlawful. Things that are themselves lawful but in whose buying and use an unlawful method is used also become forbidden, for example theft, robbery, deception, usurping rights, bribery and fraud.
  • Why the unjust killing of one human being is the killing of all humanity: the verse states the sanctity of human life and the importance of protecting it. A person becomes a killer when he breaks the bonds of human blood relations, the feeling of sympathy with humanity leaves his heart, and only his own interest remains before him, as a result of which he kills others. Therefore the unjust killing of one innocent human being is as if all humanity has been killed.

Punishments for Disturbing General Peace

  • For those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive to spread corruption in the land, four kinds of punishments have been fixed: (1) they should be killed, (2) or crucified, (3) or their hands on one side and feet on the other side should be cut off, (4) or they should be exiled from the land. That is disgrace for them in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.
  • But those who repent before you overpower them, then know that Allah Almighty is Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Al-Birr, Patience and Silah Rahmi

  • Al-Birr means goodness, and it means doing good and pleasing deeds. Its points are: (1) Beliefs: belief in Allah Almighty, the Day of Judgment, the angels, the Book of Allah Almighty and the Prophets. (2) Dealings: giving wealth, despite love for it, to relatives, orphans, the needy, travellers, and freeing slaves. (3) Acts of worship: establishing Salah and giving Zakat. (4) Morals: fulfilling a promise when made. (5) Patience: remaining steadfast at times of hardship, suffering and war. These very people are true believers, and they are those who fear Allah Almighty.
  • Three occasions of patience: (1) the time of hardship, (2) the time of suffering and calamity, (3) the time of war. On these occasions one should remain steadfast.
  • Silah Rahmi means maintaining relations with relatives and loving them and treating them well. Al-Arham is the plural of Rahm, which means blood and close relations. The Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) said: Silah Rahmi is not that when someone joins with you, you join with him; rather Silah Rahmi is that even if someone breaks with you, you still keep the close relationship joined with him.

Islamic State, Love for Allah and His Messenger, and Permission to Fight

  • In the light of verse 41 of Surah Al-Hajj, the purpose and qualities of an Islamic state are: if the believers get government, they remain firm in faith, righteous deeds, worship, avoiding shirk, striving for the dominance of the religion, and steadfastness in fear and danger. They establish Salah and also observe Zakat. They use all their authority to spread goodness and remove evil. The purpose of establishing Salah is that man's connection with Allah Almighty becomes strong and purity of soul is attained. Zakat relates to the economy of society; therefore the state should create economic resources and make proper arrangements for the needs of the people.
  • Duties of Muslim rulers after gaining power: (1) Establish Salah. (2) Pay Zakat - the state should create economic resources and make proper arrangements for the needs of the people. (3) Enjoin good and forbid evil - use all their authority to spread goodness and remove evil. (4) Provide peace and security to the subjects, and arrange for their education, health and economy. After the migration to Madinah Munawwarah, the first Islamic state came into being, for which the first constitution was made under the name of the Charter of Madinah (Mithaq-e-Madinah), and the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) was made its head and responsible for making peace among the subjects.
  • In the light of verse 24 of Surah At-Tawbah: believing in Allah, loving Allah and His Messenger, and striving (jihad) in the way of Allah come before everything in the world. Faith is the greatest wealth of the world. The standard of love of a true believer should be that his fathers, sons, friends, wives, relatives, earned wealth, trade and places of residence should not be more beloved to him than Allah and His Holy Messenger, and the love of relatives should not stop him from walking on the path of truth. If a person does not love Allah and His Holy Messenger above all, he cannot escape the displeasure of Allah Almighty.
  • Wisdom of permission to fight (izn-e-qital): to redress the oppressed, to punish the corrupt and the promise-breakers, to bring peace and security in the world, to strive for the exaltation of the word of Allah, to protect people's lives, wealth, honour and dignity, religion and the sanctity of places of worship from the evil of corrupt people, and to defend the places of worship of the heavenly religions (monasteries, churches, places of worship and mosques).
  • Condition of the Muslims in the Makkan period: the thirteen years in Makkah, from the announcement of Prophethood until the migration to Madinah, were extremely trying years of patience, trial and hardship for the Muslims and for the Holy Prophet himself. There, instead of reacting to hardships, patience was commanded, and every kind of retaliatory action was forbidden.
  • Amr bil-Ma'roof wa Nahi anil-Munkar: Ma'roof means such good and virtuous deeds which everyone calls good, and Munkar means evil deeds - that is, to enjoin good deeds and to forbid evil deeds.
  • Forms of Allah's help: (1) Allah is Able to help the oppressed Muslims, and He has promised to help the Muslims. (2) Against the cruel enemies of Islam, Allah will defend the believers. (3) Those who help the religion of Allah, Allah will surely help them. Indeed, Allah is Powerful, Mighty.

Word Meanings

  • فَلْيَسْتَعْفِفْ - He should refrain (from it).
  • مَفْرُوضًا - Made obligatory / fixed as compulsory.
  • فَارْزُقُوهُمْ - Feed them / give them.
  • ذُرِّيَّةً - Offspring (weak offspring).
  • خَافُوا - They fear.
  • بُطُونِ - Bellies.
  • سَعِيرًا - Blazing Fire.
  • لَا تَأْكُلُوا - Do not consume.
  • مُخْتَالًا - Arrogant (one who walks proudly).
  • مُسْرِفُونَ - Those who exceed limits.
  • خِزْيٌ - Disgrace.
  • تَقْدِرُوا - You overpower them / you gain control over them.
  • اِقْتَرَفْتُمْ - You earned.
  • كَرِهَ - They dislike.
  • صَوَامِعُ - Monasteries (hermitages).
  • بِيَعٌ - Churches.
  • مَكَّنَّا - We gave a place / We established.
  • الْيَتَامَى - Orphans.
  • بَثٌّ - Spread / scattered.
  • حُوبًا - Sin.
  • نِحْلَةً - Happily (as a gift).
  • السُّفَهَاءَ - The foolish / those without understanding.

chapters.title: Hadith Sharif — Introduction, Sunnah and Selected Ahadith

lessons.title: Introduction to Hadith and Sunnah and Their Effects on Practical Life
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Hadith?

  • Literal meaning: The word "Hadith" means news, talk and a new thing.
  • Technical meaning: The saying (talk), action (deed) and approval (tacit confirmation) of Prophet Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, the Seal of the Prophets (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions) is called Hadith.
  • Hadith is also called "Khabar" and "Sunnah".
  • Rawi (narrator): Each person who narrated or transmitted the hadiths from the Holy Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions) down to us is called a Rawi.
  • Sanad-e-Hadith: The chain of narrators is called Sanad-e-Hadith.
  • Matn: The text (wording) of the hadith is called Matn.

What Is Sunnah?

  • Literal meaning: "Sunnah" means "way" and "path".
  • Technical meaning: The way adopted in the life of the Holy Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions) is called Sunnah, and it also includes an act which the Holy Prophet performed repeatedly.
  • In the Holy Quran, Sunnah has been described by the name "Uswah Hasanah", which means "the best model" / "an excellent model".
  • Allah Almighty says (Surah Al-Ahzab: 21): "In the person of the Prophet there is an excellent model for you."

Difference Between Hadith and Sunnah

  • There is only a slight difference between Hadith and Sunnah.
  • Hadith is generally used for sayings.
  • Sunnah is generally used for actions and practice.
  • The word Sunnah also expresses the meaning of Hadith.

The Four Kinds of Hadith

  • (1) Hadith Qawli: The hadith in which a saying or command of the Holy Prophet is stated, as he said with his blessed tongue. Example: أَفْشُوا السَّلَامَ — "Spread salaam." (Sunan Tirmidhi, Hadith: 1854)
  • (2) Hadith Fi'li: The hadith in which an act and way of the Holy Prophet is stated, that he did thus. Example: Hazrat Anas (RA) states that the Holy Prophet drank goat's milk with yoghurt, then rinsed with water. (Sunan Ibn Majah, Hadith: 99)
  • (3) Hadith Taqriri: The hadith in which a Companion performed some act in the presence of the Holy Prophet, he knew of it, but he neither stopped him nor praised him; he remained silent, or he gave permission or expressed approval. Example: Hazrat Anas (RA) had a little brother Abu Umair who kept a nightingale (bulbul) and played with it; the Holy Prophet often came to their house but never forbade keeping that nightingale. (Sahih Bukhari: 6129, Sahih Muslim: 2150)
  • (4) Hadith Qudsi: The hadith whose meaning and purport is from Allah Almighty and whose words are those of the Holy Prophet. Example: قَالَ اللهُ: أَنْفِقْ يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ أُنْفِقْ عَلَيْكَ — "Allah said: O son of Adam! Keep spending (on My servants) and I will spend on you." (Sahih Bukhari: 5352)

Effects of Sunnah on Our Practical Life

  • Man strives to fulfil his needs and tasks, but if the Sunnah of the Prophet is observed in those tasks, those tasks are counted as deeds and worship.
  • Example: Eating and drinking is our need, but if, with the intention of Sunnah, we sit with dignity at the dastarkhwan (tablecloth) and eat together, that eating too is worship.
  • Observing the Sunnah provides for the improvement of human health and the environment, because it teaches purity and cleanliness in the use of lawful and pleasing things, which closes the door to all diseases.
  • Following the Sunnah ends differences and creates unity and agreement; when all people get a common and general code for living a practical life, the tendency to disunity among them weakens.
  • Following the Sunnah blocks the paths of false and satanic ways; the atmosphere of truth and goodness gets life, which closes the door to all social and moral evils.
  • In many matters, science too has supported the Sunnah, although the Sunnah has no need of the support of science.

Reviving the Sunnah

  • The Holy Prophet said: Whoever, at the time of corruption of my Ummah, firmly held on to any one of my Sunnahs, for him is the reward of a hundred (100) martyrs.
  • That is, the person who acts upon the Sunnah and revives it in an age of inaction and corruption gets reward equal to a hundred martyrs. (Hilyat-ul-Auliya by Al-Isbahani, Vol. 8, p. 200)

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of Hadith?
options: News, talk and a new thing
mcqs.why: The correct answer is news, talk and a new thing, which is the literal meaning of the word Hadith given in the book.

mcqs.q: What is called Sanad-e-Hadith?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the chain of narrators, because the people who narrated hadiths from the Prophet down to us are Rawis and their chain is the Sanad.

mcqs.q: What is called the Matn of a hadith?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the text of the hadith, because the book defines Matn as the wording or text of a hadith.

mcqs.q: By what name has Sunnah been described in the Holy Quran?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Uswah Hasanah, meaning the best or excellent model, as stated for Sunnah in Surah Al-Ahzab verse 21.

mcqs.q: If the meaning is from Allah Almighty and the words are those of the Holy Prophet, the hadith is called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hadith Qudsi, because in Qudsi hadith the meaning and purport is from Allah while the words are the Prophet's.

mcqs.q: The example of Abu Umair keeping a nightingale and the Prophet not forbidding it is an example of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hadith Taqriri, because a Companion did an act in the Prophet's presence, he knew of it and remained silent without forbidding it.

mcqs.q: Spread salaam (Afshu as-salaam) is an example of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hadith Qawli, because it is a saying or command spoken by the Holy Prophet with his blessed tongue.

mcqs.q: Whoever firmly holds to one Sunnah at the time of corruption of the Ummah will get the reward of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a hundred martyrs, because the hadith states that reviving a Sunnah in an age of corruption earns the reward of 100 martyrs.

mcqs.q: According to the book, following the Sunnah of the Prophet creates:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is unity and agreement, because following the Sunnah ends differences and gives all people a common code for practical life.

options: Hadith is for actions, Sunnah for sayings
There is no difference at all
Hadith is generally for sayings, Sunnah for actions and practice
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that Hadith is generally used for sayings and Sunnah for actions and practice, which is the only slight difference stated in the book.

lessons.title: Translation and Explanation of Selected Ahadith
lessons.notes_html:
Learning and Teaching the Quran, and Durood

  • خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith: 5027) — Translation: The best among you is the one who learns the Holy Quran and teaches it to others.
  • أَوْلَى النَّاسِ بِي يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ أَكْثَرُهُمْ عَلَيَّ صَلَاةً (Sunan Tirmidhi, Hadith: 484) — Translation: On the Day of Judgment, the closest person to me among the people will be the one who sends the most Durood (blessings) upon me.

Love for the Holy Prophet Is the Sign of Faith

  • لَا يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى أَكُونَ أَحَبَّ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ وَالِدِهِ وَوَلَدِهِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith: 15) — Translation: The faith of none of you is complete until I am more beloved and dear to him than his father, his children and all people.
  • Explanation: Love for the Holy Prophet has been described as the sign of faith. It includes all kinds of love, such as the love of mother, father and dear ones, or loves due to natural or psychological causes.
  • Until a person sacrifices even his own desire, will, wealth, children and life for the commands of Allah Almighty and the Holy Prophet, he is not a person of perfect faith.

Zikr, Dua and Completion of Faith

  • أَفْضَلُ الذِّكْرِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ — The best Zikr is La ilaha illallah. Zikr is also the cause of peace of heart (satisfaction of heart).
  • La ilaha illallah is the best Zikr because this Kalima is the collection of all perfect attributes, supreme in greatness and grandeur; it is the most effective in purifying the inner self and turning the heart away from every side and joining it with Allah Almighty; and by reciting it with certainty and truthfulness, man enters Islam and becomes deserving of entering Paradise.
  • Four principles of completion of faith (Sunan Abi Dawood, Hadith: 4681): (1) loving for the sake of Allah, (2) hating for the sake of Allah, (3) giving for the sake of Allah, (4) withholding for the sake of Allah. Whoever acted in this way, his faith has become complete.

Knowledge and Salah

  • طَلَبُ الْعِلْمِ فَرِيضَةٌ عَلَى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ (Sunan Ibn Majah, Hadith: 224) — Translation: Seeking knowledge is obligatory upon every Muslim. Explanation: Through knowledge the nearness of one's Creator and Master can be attained and every good and evil thing can be recognized, so that we can perform righteous deeds and avoid sins, attain beneficial things, avoid harmful things, and attain success in both worlds.
  • For seeking knowledge, going even to China has been encouraged: اُطْلُبُوا الْعِلْمَ وَلَوْ بِالصِّينِ (Kanz-ul-Ummal, Hadith: 28697, 28698).
  • اَلصَّلَاةُ عِمَادُ الدِّينِ (Ad-Durar Al-Muntashirah by As-Suyuti, 280) — Translation: Salah is the pillar of the religion. Explanation: Performing Salah five times a day is obligatory upon every sane, adult Muslim man or woman. Through Salah the servant's connection with Allah Almighty is established, and His nearness, mercy and pleasure are attained; so the five daily Salahs should be performed with great care and humility.

Foundation of Islam, Fasting and Knowledge

  • The foundation of Islam is based on five things: 1. Testimony of Tawheed and Risalah, 2. Establishing Salah, 3. Paying Zakat, 4. Keeping fasts, 5. Performing Hajj of Baitullah (agreed upon).
  • مَنْ صَامَ رَمَضَانَ إِيمَانًا وَاحْتِسَابًا غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith: 38) — Translation: Whoever kept the fasts of Ramadan with faith and with the intention of reward, all his previous sins will be forgiven.
  • Fasting is a shield from the fire of Hell (Sunan Nasa'i: 2224).
  • In Ramadan, fasting is obligatory upon every sane, adult, resident and healthy person.

Every Person Is a Guardian

  • كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith: 892) — Translation: All of you are guardians, and you will be questioned about your subjects under your care.
  • Explanation: A guardian is every person made responsible for some matters socially or in worldly terms; the people living under him are his subjects (ra'iyyat). Among his essential duties is that he is responsible for their training and reform — he teaches each of them manners and keeps them in good condition.
  • On the Day of Judgment every person will give account of his deeds, and if he had a post, position or responsibility in the world, he will also be questioned about his subordinates.

Protecting the Borders of the Homeland

  • رِبَاطُ يَوْمٍ وَلَيْلَةٍ خَيْرٌ مِنْ صِيَامِ شَهْرٍ وَقِيَامِهِ (Sahih Muslim, Hadith: 1913) — Translation: Spending one day or one night in jihad is better than fasting for a month and (performing) voluntary worship.
  • Explanation: Standing guard and protecting and watching over the borders of the country is also counted as jihad. A mujahid who defends the borders for one day or one night gets the reward of a whole month's fasts and the night Tahajjud.
  • We should be full of the spirit of jihad for the exaltation of the word of Allah and of protecting the homeland and its borders, so that no one can look at Islam, the country and the homeland with an evil eye — and in this lies success in both worlds.

Good Morals, Benefiting People and Giving

  • أَكْمَلُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِيمَانًا أَحْسَنُهُمْ خُلُقًا (Sunan Abi Dawood, Hadith: 4682) — Translation: Among you, those with perfect faith are the people whose morals are better than others. Explanation: Good morals have been described as a condition of perfect faith. The Holy Prophet said: "Among you, the most beloved to me is the one who has good morals." (Musnad Ahmad, Hadith: 6735)
  • خَيْرُ النَّاسِ أَنْفَعُهُمْ لِلنَّاسِ (Al-Jami' Al-Kabeer by As-Suyuti, Hadith: 1176) — Translation: The good person is the one who benefits people the most. Explanation: Being beneficial to people is necessary for a person to be better; the best person is beneficial to other people, whether Muslim or non-Muslim.
  • اَلْيَدُ الْعُلْيَا خَيْرٌ مِنَ الْيَدِ السُّفْلَى (Sunan Abi Dawood, Hadith: 1645) — Translation: The upper hand is better than the lower hand. Explanation: The upper hand means the giving hand and the lower hand means the taking hand. The giving hand, which provides the needy with what they need and is generous, is better and its status is very great.

Harms of Bribery

  • Bribery means every such amount or compensation through which the right of a deserving person is taken away, or something is taken in exchange for some injustice, for example unlawful gifts.
  • Taking and giving bribes is among the major sins. The Holy Prophet cursed those who take and give bribes (Sunan Abi Dawood: 3577; also Sunan Nasa'i: 2631).
  • When bribery becomes common in a nation, justice, fairness and civility end there; the unlawful demands of cruel officials become obstacles to people getting their lawful rights, and it becomes difficult for people to get their rights and concessions by lawful means.

Hajj and Sincerity (Ikhlas)

  • مَنْ حَجَّ لِلَّهِ فَلَمْ يَرْفُثْ وَلَمْ يَفْسُقْ رَجَعَ كَيَوْمِ وَلَدَتْهُ أُمُّهُ (Sahih Al-Bukhari: 1521) — Translation: Whoever performed Hajj for Allah, and then neither spoke obscenely nor abused, nor committed any sin, he returned from Hajj like the day he was born from his mother's womb. Explanation: Hajj is the last and completing pillar of Islam, obligatory once upon every sane, adult, healthy and capable person. Whoever shows patience during Hajj and stays away from vain and obscene talk, foul language, disobedience and sins becomes as clean and pure from sins as on the day of birth.
  • إِنَّ اللهَ لَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَى أَجْسَامِكُمْ وَلَا إِلَى صُوَرِكُمْ وَلَكِنْ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى قُلُوبِكُمْ (Sahih Muslim, Hadith: 2564) — Translation: Indeed, Allah Almighty does not look at your bodies and faces, but looks at your hearts. Explanation: This states the importance of sincerity (ikhlas); a person's outward and inward should be one.

Six Rights of a Muslim over a Muslim

  • لِلْمُسْلِمِ عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِ سِتٌّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ (Sunan Tirmidhi, Hadith: 2637): (1) When he meets a Muslim, he should greet him with salaam — Assalamu Alaikum; (2) when he invites him, he should accept it; (3) when he sneezes, he should say Yarhamukallah (May Allah have mercy on you); (4) when he is sick, he should visit him; (5) when he dies, he should join his funeral; (6) whatever he likes for himself, he should like for the other too.
  • This creates a shared bond between two Muslims and strengthens it. Allah says: "Believers are brothers among themselves." (Surah Al-Hujurat: 10)

Branches of Faith and Haya

  • The highest branch of faith is saying La ilaha illallah, because through it alone the affirmation of Tawheed takes place.
  • The last (lowest) branch is removing a harmful thing from the path. (Sahih Muslim, Hadith: 35)
  • Haya (modesty) is a branch of faith.

Guiding to Good, Avoiding Suspicion, Helping the Needy

  • مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى خَيْرٍ فَلَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِ فَاعِلِهِ (Sahih Muslim, Hadith: 1893) — Translation: Whoever guided a person towards goodness, he too will get the same reward as the one who does the good deed. Through good advice, guidance, and education and training, the helper gets as much reward as the doer.
  • إِيَّاكُمْ وَالظَّنَّ فَإِنَّ الظَّنَّ أَكْذَبُ الْحَدِيثِ (Sahih Bukhari, Hadith: 6066) — Translation: Beware of suspicion; suspicion is the biggest lie.
  • مَنْ نَفَّسَ عَنْ مُؤْمِنٍ كُرْبَةً مِنْ كُرَبِ الدُّنْيَا نَفَّسَ اللهُ عَنْهُ كُرْبَةً مِنْ كُرَبِ يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ، مَنْ يَسَّرَ عَلَى مُعْسِرٍ يَسَّرَ اللهُ عَلَيْهِ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ (Sahih Muslim, Hadith: 2699) — Translation: Whoever removed any of the worldly hardships of a believer, Allah will save him from hardships on the Day of Judgment; and whoever gave any facility to a person in difficulty, Allah will create ease for him in this world and the Hereafter.
  • Helping includes removing a believer's hardship, serving and financially helping the needy, sick, poor and destitute, and giving a debtor respite in his loan.

Neighbours, Guests and Relatives

  • Three kinds of neighbours (Surah An-Nisa: 36): 1. A neighbour who is a relative, 2. One who is only a neighbour, 3. One who stayed with you temporarily for some time — for example a classmate, or a companion of a meeting, a journey, or some gathering. Good conduct should be shown to all neighbours.
  • The benefit of Silah Rahmi stated in the hadith is abundance of sustenance and long life (Sahih Bukhari, Hadith: 2027).

Word Meanings and Key Terms

  • Zikrullah: In its broad meaning it includes Salah, recitation of the Quran, dua and istighfar; generally, describing the glorification and sanctification of Allah Almighty, His Oneness and purity, His greatness and grandeur, and His perfect attributes is called Zikrullah.
  • Dua: The expression of humility by a weak person when asking from one superior to himself; supplicating in the court of Allah Almighty while believing Him to be All-Powerful, and presenting a request. Dua is a means of attaining one's objective.
  • Husn-e-Akhlaq (good morals): In living life and observing the principles and rules of the religion, treating others well instead of causing them pain, behaving gently, and carrying out one's responsibilities happily while helping them financially.
  • Ikhlas (sincerity): Whatever good deed is done should be done only to attain the pleasure of Allah Almighty, with no worldly motive, show-off, desire for fame, or motive of any compensation; a person's outward and inward should be one. A deed done for the pleasure of Allah is called Ikhlas.
  • Haya (modesty): Such a quality and characteristic of a person which stops a person from immorality, and from many evils and sins; Haya is an important branch of faith.
  • Zann: Saying something about someone by guesswork, without investigation and certain knowledge, is called Zann or suspicion.
  • Husn-e-Zann: If goodness is intended in Zann, it is Husn-e-Zann (good opinion), a pleasing quality which has been encouraged; keeping Husn-e-Zann with Allah Almighty is worship, and the Holy Prophet said Husn-e-Zann is good worship (Musnad Ahmad, Hadith: 7956).
  • Badgumani (bad suspicion): Holding an evil opinion about someone — doubting someone's intention and not keeping a good thought about him without reason. It is forbidden in the Quran: "O believers! Avoid suspicions, for that is a sinful act." (Surah Al-Hujurat: 12) Gradually suspicion turns into hatred and enmity of hearts, which is a sin.
  • Fard-e-Ain: Every person, whether man or woman, must learn that much knowledge through which he understands the necessary matters of belief, lawful and unlawful, pure and impure, permissible and impermissible, and his responsibilities.
  • Fard-e-Kifayah: Acquiring the complete knowledge of the religion, and acquiring worldly sciences and arts, is Fard-e-Kifayah.
  • Ikram-uz-Zaif (honouring the guest): When a person travels and reaches someone for some purpose, he is a guest; asking him the purpose of his coming properly, behaving respectfully, arranging his lodging, food and drink and rest, and honouring him according to his status is honouring the guest.
  • Silah Rahmi: Sharing in the joys and sorrows of one's close dear ones and relatives, helping them in times of need, treating them well, and sympathising with them.
  • Signs of a good person: He benefits others, does not cause them pain, and arranges for their food, drink and other facilities — whether they are Muslim or non-Muslim.

lessons.title: Aqeedah Tauheed (Belief in the Oneness of Allah)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Tawheed

  • The literal meaning of the word "Tawheed" is "to consider One and to believe as One".
  • In the terminology of religion, Tawheed means that the Creator, Master and Controller of everything in this universe is Allah Almighty alone.
  • He is only One; He has no partner.
  • Believing this belief with firm conviction of the heart, and expressing and confessing it with the tongue when needed and at the right time, is called the belief of Tawheed.

Allah Almighty — Creator and True God

  • Allah Almighty has always existed and will always remain; He alone is the true object of worship.
  • He created everything of this universe in balance and its system with complete calculation.
  • He has knowledge of every particle of the universe; His sight is over the whole universe.
  • He hears all, provides sustenance to all, and guides them.
  • There is none like Him or equal to Him; He alone is the Master of the benefit and harm of creation.
  • There is none besides Him; He alone will give everlasting life again after death.

Allah is Eternal (Azali) and Everlasting (Abadi)

  • هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ (Surah Al-Hadid, verse: 3).
  • When there was nothing, He still existed; and in the end too, there will be nothing, but He will exist.
  • He has always existed and will always remain. No one created Him.

Meaning of Iman

  • By Aqeedah are meant those thoughts and ideas in which man holds firm belief, which affect man's character and behaviour.
  • The meaning of Iman is also this same firm belief.

What is Ibadat (Worship)?

  • Reserving all those deeds for Allah Almighty which come under worship is called Ibadat.
  • For example: worshipping none besides Him, vows and offerings also being for Him, asking duas from Him, seeking refuge from Him, and calling upon Him alone for unseen help.

Requirements of Tawheed

  • (1) The Being of Allah Almighty is without example. Nothing in the universe is like Allah Almighty: "There is nothing like Him" (Surah Ash-Shura, verse: 11). So Allah Almighty should be believed as an unparalleled Being.
  • (2) Only Allah Almighty is the One for whose pleasure man should strive.
  • (3) All deeds that come under worship should be reserved for Allah Almighty alone.
  • (4) All emotions and feelings should be reserved for Allah Almighty alone, in which the spirit of worship is found: Hamd, Shukr, hope, Tawakkul, fear, Taqwa, true love, devotion, humility and submission, etc.
  • (5) The true Supreme Ruler of this whole universe should be believed to be Allah Almighty alone. The true Lawgiver is also He alone. Making laws for the life of creation, forgiving them or punishing them is His right alone.
  • (6) Life should be spent in this world according to the guidance and command sent by Allah Almighty.
  • (7) Faith should be brought in Allah Almighty along with all His attributes.

Effects of the Belief in Tawheed

  • Believing in the names and attributes of Allah Almighty creates love and reverence for Allah Almighty in the servant's heart, as a result of which he becomes obedient to the commands of Allah Almighty.
  • Tawheed grants man the highest station of freedom and liberty.
  • It creates qualities like piety, self-respect and self-honour in man, and it creates humility and humbleness in man.
  • Man looks at the whole creation with love and affection with a broad outlook, because it is the creation of Allah Almighty.
  • It creates in man the power of steadfastness, courage, contentment, needfulness, determination, patience and Tawakkul.
  • Because of complete trust in the mercy of Allah Almighty, he never becomes disappointed and hopeless.
  • It creates in man the concept of the unity and equality of mankind.

First Duty and Basis of Salvation

  • A Muslim should first of all correct his belief.
  • The basis of man's welfare and salvation is faith and good deeds.

lessons.title: Aqeedah Risalat (Belief in Prophethood)
lessons.notes_html:
Literal Meaning of Nubuwwat and Risalah

  • "Nubuwwat" is derived from the word "Naba", which means news. The one who gives news is called "Nabi", whose plural is Anbiya.
  • "Risalah" means conveying the message, and the one who conveys the message is called "Rasool", whose plural is "Rusul".
  • So, the one who gives news is called a "Nabi", and the one who conveys the message is called a "Rasool"; the person who holds the office of Nubuwwat and Risalah is called a Nabi or Rasool.

Technical Meaning of Nubuwwat and Risalah

  • In the terminology of religion, "Nubuwwat and Risalah" is a high spiritual office, for which Allah Almighty chooses special servants from among His servants.
  • Through it, human beings attain the knowledge of Allah (Ma'rifat-e-Ilahi).
  • It is an office which works to establish a connection between Allah Almighty and His servants.
  • Through it, Allah Almighty conveys His commands and guidance to His servants; through it, He guides, reforms and trains human beings.
  • Even before receiving Risalah, the status of a Rasool in his nation is high and exalted. He is innocent, pure, soft-spoken, of good nature, truthful and trustworthy.
  • Nubuwwat and Risalah is an office which Allah Almighty grants to His specially chosen servants.

The Belief in Risalah

  • The belief in Risalah is the second important and basic belief of Islam.
  • Believing in the Nabi and Rasool is obligatory.
  • The Holy Quran says: كُلٌّ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ رُسُلِهِ (Surah Al-Baqarah: 285). Translation: All believe in Allah, His angels, His books and His Prophets, and say: we make no distinction between any of His Prophets.
  • Allah Almighty sent a Prophet for the guidance and leadership of every nation, and the first Prophet sent by Allah Almighty is Hazrat Adam (AS).

Why Nubuwwat and Risalah are Needed

  • The purpose of man's creation and life has been stated as "the servitude and obedience of Allah Almighty", and on this depends man's success and salvation in this world and the Hereafter.
  • Man naturally wants an example or model for practical life, and the lives of the Prophets are the best example or an excellent model of conduct for human beings.
  • Allah Almighty sends down a book upon the Prophets for the guidance of His servants.
  • This world is the place of action, and the Hereafter is the place of accountability and questioning.
  • Just as Allah Almighty has arranged to fulfil man's physical needs, in the same way He arranged Nubuwwat and Risalah to fulfil spiritual needs.

Obedience (Ita'at) and Following (Ittiba)

  • Ita'at is derived from the word "Taw'", which means the inclination of the heart and obeying or accepting a command.
  • In obedience, one has to submit oneself completely; it cannot be that some commands are obeyed and some are not. The attitude of accepting firm obedience with the attachment of the heart is called Ita'at.
  • Ittiba is following every step and every manner of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions) with true love of the heart, complete inclination of nature, and deep attachment — that is, when heartfelt love is joined with complete obedience, it is called Ittiba.
  • Obedience to the Messenger is that in all matters of life, whatever commands he gave, or guidance he gave, or whatever act he performed, it should be obeyed and acted upon.
  • Allah Almighty does not speak directly to His servants; He speaks only through His Messenger, and the Messenger informs the servants of Allah Almighty's guidance and commands. So obedience to the Messenger is in fact obedience to Allah Almighty.
  • The Holy Quran says: "Whoever obeyed the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions), indeed he obeyed Allah." (Surah An-Nisa, verse: 80).

Our Four Relationships with the Holy Prophet ﷺ

  • Our four basic relationships with the Holy Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions) are: (1) Iman, (2) obedience, (3) following, and (4) love.
  • The chain of Nubuwwat was completed with the Holy Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions), and the belief in the Finality of Prophethood (Khatm-e-Nubuwwat) is an essential part of faith.

Love for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ

  • Hubb or love is a natural attraction and a natural feeling; if this love is on the basis of a religious relationship, it is called "spiritual love" or "faith-based love".
  • The Holy Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions) is the Beloved of Allah Almighty and the benefactor and guide of the believers, so he deserves every kind of love from us, and it is also a requirement of faith.
  • In the sight of Allah Almighty, that faith and obedience is not even credible whose foundation is not upon the love of the Messenger of Allah.
  • The standard of this love is that the Holy Prophet deserves more love than even their own lives (Al-Ahzab: 6).
  • Love for the Messenger has been declared the sign of faith, and it is the sign of perfect faith: "None of you can be a believer until he loves me more than his parents, children and all people." (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Kitab-ul-Iman, Hadith: 15).

Belief in Khatm-e-Nubuwwat (Finality of Prophethood)

  • The literal meaning of "Khatm" is to seal and to complete a task and be free from it.
  • The chain of Nubuwwat began with Hazrat Adam (AS), many Prophets came one after another, and it ended with the Holy Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions). Now no Prophet will come after him.
  • With Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions), the chain of Nubuwwat was completed, and the religion became complete.
  • اَلْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ الْإِسْلَامَ دِينًا (Al-Ma'idah: 3). Translation: Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favours upon you, and chosen Islam as the religion for you.
  • مَا كَانَ مُحَمَّدٌ أَبَا أَحَدٍ مِنْ رِجَالِكُمْ وَلَكِنْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَخَاتَمَ النَّبِيِّينَ (Surah Al-Ahzab: 40). Translation: Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions) is not the father of any of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets.
  • The Holy Prophet said: In my Ummah, (30) thirty such liars will come, each of whom will claim to be a Prophet, whereas I am the last Prophet; there is no Prophet after me. (Abu Dawood, Hadith 4253).
  • When the religion became complete and the Holy Prophet was announced as the last Prophet and Messenger, there remained no need for any new Prophet.
  • Therefore, whoever claims Prophethood in any way after the Holy Prophet is a disbeliever and out of the fold of Islam.

Characteristics of the Last Risalah

  • Universality and worldwide scope.
  • Renewal of the earlier Shariahs.
  • Completeness.
  • Protection of the Book.
  • Protection of the Sunnah of the Prophet.
  • Comprehensiveness, and the Finality of Prophethood (Khatm-e-Nubuwwat).

lessons.title: Importance and Benefits of Worship
lessons.notes_html:
What Ibadat Means

  • Ibadat is an Arabic word derived from "Abd".
  • Its literal meaning is: servitude, humility, humbleness, obedience and submission.
  • Its Shariah (technical) meaning is: living one's life according to the Uswah Hasanah of the Holy Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions), with the intention of attaining the pleasure of Allah Almighty.
  • Ibadat includes every act which Allah Almighty has commanded to do, or forbidden to do, because it is the servant's job to obey his Master.
  • If that Master is the King of kings, then considering His commands as a cause of happiness, joy and contentment for oneself is the highest achievement of a servant.

Importance of Ibadat

  • In Islam, after the correctness of faith or belief, emphasis has been laid on Ibadat.
  • These acts of worship are the practical form of direct contact, connection and nearness with Allah Almighty.
  • Allah Almighty says: "And I created the jinn and mankind only that they may worship Me" (Az-Zariyat: 56).
  • Allah Almighty says: "O mankind! Worship your Lord who created you and those before you, so that you may be saved (from His punishment)" (Surah Al-Baqarah: 21).

Purpose of Ibadat — Taqwa

  • In Surah Al-Baqarah: 21, the purpose of Ibadat has been stated as "Taqwa".
  • Taqwa is the stage after the purity of the heart, the cleanliness of the soul, and the sincerity of action.
  • It is that heartfelt condition of man, by which the desire to do good deeds and hatred for evils is created.
  • Allah says: قُلْ إِنَّ صَلَاتِي وَنُسُكِي وَمَحْيَايَ وَمَمَاتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ — "Say: my Salah and my sacrifice, and my living and my dying are all for Allah, the Lord of the worlds" (Surah Al-An'am: 162).
  • This verse presents a brief and comprehensive outline of the straight path (Sirat-e-Mustaqeem), which is the soul of Islamic life and the life of Islamic society.
  • Every breath, every step and every deed of a Muslim is for Allah Almighty — not for anyone besides Allah or for the desires of one's own self; this is the purpose and intent of a Muslim's life.

Requirements of Ibadat

  • Accept all the commands of Allah Almighty and act upon them.
  • Leave whatever He has declared forbidden.
  • Fulfil whatever He has declared obligatory and compulsory, thus obeying Allah Almighty completely.
  • Bring every sphere of life within the circle of the obedience of Allah Almighty — that is, observe complete obedience.
  • Allah Almighty says: "O believers! Enter Islam completely" (Al-Baqarah: 208).

Effects of Ibadat on General Life

  • It creates feelings of love and sympathy for mankind, so a Muslim keeps love and affection for other people, sympathises with them, and helps them in their joys and sorrows.
  • It teaches patience and tolerance, and creates the spirit of sacrificing one's personal interest for the pleasure of Allah Almighty and the collective benefit.
  • It teaches living together with society, so man learns to live together with other people, and society becomes likeable.
  • Observing Ibadat ends bad habits like laziness, idleness and wasting time.
  • By observing Salah, qualities of punctuality, outward and inward purity and cleanliness, obedience to the leader, and collectivity are created in man, and he is saved from immodesty and shamelessness.
  • Fasting creates Taqwa in man — that is, the fear of God makes man distinguish between good and evil.
  • Through Zakat, the love of wealth decreases in man, and he feels happiness in helping financially people like himself.
  • Hajj teaches the lesson of collectivity on a worldwide level.
  • Acts like helping people, Silah Rahmi, and supporting the people under one's care improve mutual interaction and relations.
  • These effects are attained by the believer on the basis of his intention and sincerity; correctness of intention and sincerity in Ibadat are the key to its acceptance.
  • These acts of worship, along with the reform of man, become the means of spreading goodness and virtues in society, and the cause of worldly and Hereafter prosperity for the believer.

lessons.title: Jihad — Introduction, Importance and Types
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning and Concept of Jihad

  • Jihad is an Arabic word derived from "Juhd".
  • Its literal meaning is: hard work, struggle, much effort and striving.
  • In Shariah terms, it is every struggle and effort for the pleasure of Allah Almighty, which is for the exaltation and protection of the religion of Allah Almighty, and the protection and defence of the country and nation.
  • It also includes every effort and struggle for the reform of society, to establish goodness and virtue, and to end evils and corruptions.

Virtue and Importance of Jihad

  • Islam has given great virtue and importance to Jihad, because ending killing, corruption, oppression and every kind of evil in the world, which becomes the cause of fitnah and corruption within society, and establishing an atmosphere of peace and security in the world, and protecting human rights, is possible only through Jihad.
  • Allah says: وَجَاهِدُوا بِأَمْوَالِكُمْ وَأَنْفُسِكُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ ذَلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ — "And strive in the way of Allah with your wealth and your lives; that is better for you, if you know" (At-Tawbah: 41).
  • The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions) said: The person who died in such a state that in his life he neither practically performed Jihad nor desired Jihad, died at the level of hypocrisy (Sahih Muslim: 1910).
  • The believer himself should remain firm on truth, speak the truth, and persuade others to remain firm on truth; keeping striving for the exaltation of truth is called Afdal-ul-Jihad.
  • The Holy Messenger (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions) said: أَفْضَلُ الْجِهَادِ كَلِمَةُ عَدْلٍ عِنْدَ سُلْطَانٍ جَائِرٍ — that is, speaking a word of truth before a cruel ruler is the best Jihad (Sunan Abi Dawood: 4344).

Objectives of Jihad

  • The basic objectives are: establishing an atmosphere of peace and security in the world, and protecting human rights.
  • Jihad fi Sabeelillah is that everything should be done only for the pleasure of Allah Almighty, so that the religion of Allah Almighty is established on His earth.
  • Special objective (a) — Punishment for breaking a treaty: Islam lays great emphasis on fulfilling treaties; the command has been given to fight that nation which makes a treaty with the Islamic government not to wage war, and then keeps warlike intentions behind that treaty.
  • Special objective (b) — Respect for humanity and help of the oppressed: supporting and helping the oppressed, and freeing them from the oppression of the oppressors, has been declared obligatory for the Islamic government.
  • Special objective (c) — Ending fitnah and corruption: restoring peace, spreading love and tolerance, and ending oppression, fitnah and corruption.

Kind 1 — Jihad Against the Desires of the Self

  • The inner power that stops man from the obedience and worship of Allah Almighty is his Nafs-e-Ammarah, which incites man towards sins, evils and disobedience.
  • It includes self-liking, hatred, backbiting, lying and foul language, and the domination of other desires of the self, which can spoil man's deeds and character.
  • Keeping this Nafs-e-Ammarah under control comes under the category of Jihad.
  • Allah says: "And whoever fears standing before his Lord and restrains himself from the desire of his self, for him the everlasting abode is Paradise" (Surah An-Nazi'at: 40).
  • The Holy Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions) declared that person who controls his self a Mujahid: الْمُجَاهِدُ مَنْ جَاهَدَ نَفْسَهُ (Sunan Tirmidhi: 1621).
  • In some narrations, Jihad with the self has been called Jihad-e-Akbar.

Kind 2 — Jihad to End Evils

  • When individual evils become common, they together take the form of collective corruption; Islam has named all these evils "Munkarat".
  • Munkarat includes oppression and excess, theft, gambling, behaviour based on verbal and national pride, false testimonies, stubbornness and bribery, adulteration, shortfall in weights and measures, corrupt customs, violation of the rights of the deserving, and usury, etc.
  • To end Munkarat and reform society, the Holy Quran has mentioned different ways: sometimes Amr bil-Ma'roof wa Nahi anil-Munkar, sometimes Dawah and Tableegh, and sometimes the advice of truth and patience.
  • The blessed hadith is: مَنْ رَأَى مِنْكُمْ مُنْكَرًا فَلْيُغَيِّرْهُ بِيَدِهِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَبِلِسَانِهِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَبِقَلْبِهِ — "Whoever sees an evil, he should remove it with his hand; if he cannot remove it with his hand, then with his tongue; if he cannot do so even with his tongue, then he should consider it evil in his heart" (Sahih Muslim: 49).

Kind 3 — Jihad bis-Saif / Armed Jihad (Qital)

  • Jihad bis-Saif means Jihad with the sword.
  • If an enemy power attacks an Islamic country, then fighting for the protection of its borders and the religion, faith, life and wealth, honour and dignity of its citizens is obligatory upon that country.
  • For defence, Allah Almighty gave the Muslims permission for armed Jihad: "Those Muslims who are fought against have permission to fight too, because they are being wronged. And Allah Almighty will help them, and indeed He is Able to help them" (Al-Hajj: 39).
  • There are three kinds of Jihad in total.

Conditions of Armed Jihad

  • (a) I'la-e-Kalimatullah (exaltation of the religion of Allah Almighty): the first condition is that it should be only for the exaltation of the religion of Allah Almighty.
  • (b) Declaration by the Islamic state: the declaration of Qital should be by the state; in Islam, only and only the state is authorised to declare Qital. The declaration or fatwa (for war) of any individual or group has no Shariah status; rather, such a declaration or fatwa comes under the category of "Fasad fil-Ard".
  • (c) Suitable military strength should be available: the Islamic government should have suitable strength and power to fight the opposing force, and the Holy Quran emphasises keeping the Islamic state strong and preparing strength and ready horses to strike awe into the enemies.
  • (d) Ignorant ways should not be used in fighting: fight only those who are armed in opposition and keep trying to fight; hands should not be raised against women, children, old people, the wounded and ordinary citizens; the dead of the enemy should not be mutilated; fields, crops, houses and cattle should not be destroyed unnecessarily.

chapters.title: Seerat Tayyaba — Baasat, Dawat, Hijrat, Ghazwat and Shamail

lessons.title: Baasat-e-Nabawi ﷺ (The Beginning of Prophethood)
lessons.notes_html:
What is Baasat-e-Nabawi?

  • The blessed age of the Holy Prophet ﷺ had reached forty years.
  • He was engaged, as usual, in solitude and worship in the Cave of Hira in the month of Ramadan.
  • Jibraeel (AS) came to him by the command of Allah Almighty and blessed him with Nubuwwat and Risalah through revelation.
  • This is Baasat-e-Nabawi.

The First Revelation

  • The first verses revealed were the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq (Al-Alaq: 1–5).
  • They begin with the command: Read in the name of your Sustainer who created.
  • Man was created from a clot of blood; Allah is the Most Generous.
  • He taught by the pen and taught man what he did not know.
  • The mention of reading and the pen shows that education and teaching are a purpose of Baasat.

Signs Before Baasat

  • Six years before Baasat, the Holy Prophet ﷺ began to see a light and brightness, with no sound, and seeing it he became extremely happy.
  • Revelation began with true dreams. Hazrat Aisha (RA) narrated in Bukhari Sharif that his night dreams came true like the light of the morning.
  • Stones and trees in Makkah greeted him: Assalamu Alaika Ya Rasulullah — O Messenger of Allah, peace be upon you.
  • He said: I recognise a stone in Makkah which used to greet me before Baasat (Sahih Muslim: 2277).
  • An extraordinary event contrary to habit that points to Prophethood is called a miracle and is counted among the signs of Prophethood.

Arabia Before Baasat

  • Makkah was the big city of Arabia and the spiritual and social centre of the Quraysh, equal to Sanaa of Yemen.
  • Quraysh caravans travelled twice a year to Syria and Yemen.
  • Qusayy bin Kilab, grandfather in the fifth generation, set up the administration of Makkah; the consultative council was called Dar-un-Nadwah.
  • Evils were common: usury, gambling, theft, drinking, oppression, burying daughters alive, and idol-worship.
  • Inside the Kabatullah alone there were 360 idols. The Quran describes corruption on land and sea (Ar-Room: 41).

Four Objectives of Baasat

  • Reciting and conveying the verses of Allah to the people.
  • Purifying human beings.
  • Teaching them the Book.
  • Teaching them matters of wisdom (Al-Jumuah: 2).
  • So the Holy Prophet ﷺ was a preacher, a teacher, a guide and a reformer.

mcqs.q: At what age did the Holy Prophet ﷺ receive Baasat (Prophethood)?

mcqs.why: The correct answer is Ramadan-ul-Mubarak. The lesson states he was worshipping in the Cave of Hira in the month of Ramadan at the time of Baasat.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is Al-Alaq. The first revealed verses are Surah Al-Alaq verses 1 to 5, beginning with Iqra Bismi Rabbik — Read in the name of your Sustainer.

mcqs.q: According to the first revelation, by what means did Allah teach man?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is by the pen. Surah Al-Alaq verse 4 says He taught by the pen, and verse 5 says He taught man what he did not know.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is six years. The lesson states that six years before Baasat he began to see a light and brightness in which there was no sound.

mcqs.q: Who narrated that revelation began with true dreams?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Aisha (RA). Bukhari Sharif narrates from Umm-ul-Mumineen Hazrat Aisha (RA) that revelation began with true dreams that came true like morning light.

mcqs.q: What did the stones and trees of Makkah say to the Holy Prophet ﷺ before Baasat?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Assalamu Alaika Ya Rasulullah, meaning O Messenger of Allah, peace be upon you. The lesson says this voice came from stones and trees as he passed.

mcqs.q: The Quraysh caravans travelled twice a year to which two lands?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Syria and Yemen. The lesson states the trade caravans of the Quraysh travelled twice a year to Syria and Yemen.
