mcqs.why: The correct answer is 360 idols. The lesson states that inside the Kabatullah alone three hundred and sixty idols were placed due to widespread ignorance and idol-worship.

lessons.title: Dawat and Tabligh (Invitation and Preaching)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Dawah and Tableegh

  • Dawah literally means calling and summoning; Tableegh means conveying.
  • Calling people towards Islam and religious teaching is Dawah-e-Deen.
  • Conveying its matters fully to other people, nations and countries with goodwill and zeal is Tableegh.
  • Allah says: Who can be better in speech than the one who calls towards Allah and does righteous deeds (Fussilat: 33).

Two Stages in Makkah

  • First stage: secret Tableegh for three years after Baasat, preaching Tawheed with silence and secrecy.
  • First believers: among men Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA), among women Hazrat Khadijah (RA), among slaves Zaid bin Harith (RA), among children Hazrat Ali (RA).
  • The house of Hazrat Arqam near Mount Safa was the gathering place and centre, where Muslims learned the Quran and offered Salah.
  • Second stage: open and public Tableegh, begun with the command: Warn your close relatives (Ash-Shuara: 214).
  • He invited the family of his grandfather Abdul Muttalib, then addressed the people from Mount Safa, and was later commanded to invite the whole nation and all human beings (Saba: 28).

Three Principles (An-Nahl: 125)

  • Call to the way of your Sustainer with wisdom and good advice, and debate in the best manner.
  • Wisdom (Hikmah): speaking according to the audience environment and understanding, with suitable scholarly and rational arguments.
  • Good advice (Mauizah Hasanah): stating good and evil kindly, without hurting the heart, to convince for the truth.
  • Debate in the best manner: strong arguments in a soft tone, avoiding anger, excitement and bitter talk.
  • The preacher must himself act upon what he preaches to others.

Objectives of Dawah and Tableegh

  • Convey the message of Allah to the people.
  • Believe Allah as One Lord and make no partner with Him in His Being, attributes, powers and rights.
  • Consider Islam the true religion and oneself answerable before Allah.
  • Believe in the Prophets and follow them; follow the Seerah of the last Prophet ﷺ, promote goodness and end evils.

Effects of Dawah and Tableegh

  • Suwaid bin Samit of Madinah heard Quranic verses in the Hajj season and became convinced of the truth of Islam; within three years many people of Madinah entered Islam.
  • Migration to Madinah followed; a mosque was founded and peace treaties were made with surrounding tribes.
  • After Badr, Uhud, Khandaq and Hudaybiyyah, preaching letters were written to kings and Khaybar was conquered, then Makkah was conquered.
  • At Hajjat-ul-Wida, more than one hundred thousand Companions (RA) were ready for Hajj.

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of Dawah?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is calling. The lesson states that in Arabic the literal meaning of Dawah is calling and summoning, while Tableegh means conveying.

mcqs.q: Conveying a good and virtuous matter to others is called what?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Tableegh. The lesson defines Tableegh as conveying the matters of religion fully to other people, nations and countries with goodwill and zeal.

mcqs.q: How long did the secret stage of Tableegh last after Baasat?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is three years. The lesson states the first stage was secret Tableegh for the period of three years after Baasat, spent preaching Tawheed with silence and secrecy.

mcqs.q: Who was the first among men to accept Islam in the secret stage?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA). The lesson lists first believers as Abu Bakr among men, Khadijah among women, Zaid bin Harith among slaves and Ali among children.

mcqs.q: What was the initial centre of Dawah and Tableegh in Makkah?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Dar-e-Arqam, the house of Hazrat Arqam near Mount Safa. Muslims gathered there to learn the Holy Quran and offer Salah.

mcqs.q: Which verse commanded the open stage: Warn your close relatives?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Surah Ash-Shuara: 214. After this command to warn close relatives, he invited the family of Abdul Muttalib and began open preaching.

mcqs.q: What are the three principles of Dawah in Surah An-Nahl: 125?
options: Wisdom, good advice and best-manner debate
mcqs.why: The correct answer is wisdom, good advice and best-manner debate. An-Nahl: 125 commands calling with Hikmah and Mauizah Hasanah and debating in the manner which is best.

mcqs.q: What must a Dai (preacher) do about what he preaches?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is act upon it himself. The lesson states it is necessary that the one who does Dawah himself acts upon the matter he preaches to others.

mcqs.q: Who heard Quranic verses in the Hajj season and became convinced of Islam, affecting Yathrib?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Suwaid bin Samit. Famous for bravery and poetry, he heard verses from the Holy Prophet ﷺ and became convinced of the truth of Islam.

mcqs.q: How should the Dai respond to the criticism of the audience?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is overlook it. The lesson teaches debate in a soft tone without anger, and the book MCQ confirms the Dai should overlook criticism.

lessons.title: Hijrat-e-Madinah and Ghazwat (Migration to Madinah and the Battles)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Hijrah

  • Hijrah literally means separation, parting, and leaving one place forever for another.
  • In Islam it means leaving homeland and relatives for the pleasure of Allah and settling elsewhere, especially when oppressed and unable to practise Islam freely.

Causes of Migration to Madinah

  • Great oppression of Muslims in Makkah, including three years locked up and boycotted in Shib-e-Abi Talib and the martyrdom of several Companions.
  • Dawah became extremely difficult after Quraysh, who once called him Sadiq and Ameen, became his mortal enemies.
  • The encouraging experience of migration to Abyssinia, where Companions found comfort.
  • The eagerness of the people of Madinah, who pledged Bayat twice at Aqabah and wished him to come to Yathrib.
  • Divine command: permission was given on 27 Safar in the 14th year of Baasat; this migration was obligatory on all Muslims.

The Hijrah Journey

  • Quraysh disbelievers plotted in Dar-un-Nadwah out of jealousy, as Aws and Khazraj had become supporters of the Muslims.
  • Hazrat Ali (RA) was seated on his bed so the trusts of the disbelievers could be returned safely to their owners.
  • With Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA) he stayed three days in the Cave of Thawr; on the fourth day Abdullah bin Uraiqit was hired as guide.
  • He reached Quba in year 14 of Prophethood, i.e. 1 Hijri, rested, and built Masjid-e-Quba, whose foundation was on piety.
  • On Friday he led Jumuah Salah at Banu Salim bin Awf in the valley of Batan, then entered Madinah to an enthusiastic welcome.

Ghazwah and the Main Battles

  • Ghazwah means going out to fight; it is an expedition in which the Holy Prophet ﷺ himself participated as commander for the exaltation of the word of Allah.
  • Badr: Ramadan 2 Hijri, under Abu Jahl the polytheists intended to attack Madinah; 313 Muslims defeated 1000 disbelievers; 70 disbelievers killed and 70 taken prisoner.
  • Uhud: Shawwal 3 Hijri under Abu Sufyan; Muslims suffered great loss but the enemy did not succeed.
  • Khandaq (Ahzab): Dhu-ul-Qadah 5 Hijri; a storm and severe wind ruined the attackers plans.
  • Khaybar 7 Hijri: last fort Qamoos conquered under Hazrat Ali (RA). Conquest of Makkah Ramadan 8 Hijri; Hunayn 8 Hijri; Tabuk 9 Hijri, Romans withdrew without fighting.

Virtue of Hijrah

  • Migrants gain benefit in this world and the Hereafter, Allah mercy, forgiveness, Paradise and the best reward (Aal-e-Imran: 195).
  • Until Jihad became obligatory, Hijrah was the greatest deed.
  • After the Conquest of Makkah, Hijrah is Mustahab (recommended), provided it is in the way of Allah and for firmness on religion and its Dawah.

mcqs.q: What is the meaning of the word Hijrah?
options: Migrating for the sake of religion
mcqs.why: The correct answer is migrating for the sake of religion. Hijrah means leaving homeland for the pleasure of Allah when oppressed and unable to practise Islam freely.

mcqs.q: During the Hijrah journey, the Holy Prophet ﷺ stayed for rest in which cave?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Cave of Thawr. He and Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA) stayed inside the Cave of Thawr for three days during the migration.

mcqs.q: Who was seated on the bed of the Holy Prophet ﷺ on the night of Hijrah to return the trusts?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Ali (RA). He was seated on the bed so the trusts of the disbelievers kept with the Prophet ﷺ could be delivered safely to their owners.

mcqs.q: Who was hired as guide after leaving the Cave of Thawr?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Abdullah bin Uraiqit. On the fourth day he was taken on hire to show the way from the Cave of Thawr towards Madinah.

mcqs.q: The mosque built at Quba during Hijrah is called what?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Masjid-e-Quba. He built it at Quba and offered Salah in it, and the Quran praises the mosque founded on piety from the first day.

mcqs.q: An expedition in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself participated is called what?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Ghazwah. According to Muhadditheen and Seerah writers, a Ghazwah is the expedition in which the Holy Prophet ﷺ himself participated as commander.

mcqs.q: When did Ghazwa Badr take place and under whose leadership did the enemy come?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Ramadan 2 Hijri under Abu Jahl. The lesson states the polytheists under Abu Jahl intended to attack Madinah and were defeated at Badr.

mcqs.q: How many Muslims and disbelievers were there at Badr?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 313 Muslims and 1000 disbelievers. The Muslims won; 70 disbelievers were killed and 70 were made prisoners.

mcqs.q: Which Ghazwah is the second Ghazwah, fought in Shawwal 3 Hijri under Abu Sufyan?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Uhud. One year after Badr, the polytheists under Abu Sufyan attacked in Shawwal 3 Hijri and were confronted at Uhud.

mcqs.q: After the Conquest of Makkah, what is the ruling of Hijrah according to the lesson?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Mustahab, recommended. The lesson says after the Conquest of Makkah Hijrah is not obligatory but recommended, if it is in the way of Allah.

lessons.title: Khasail and Shamail-e-Nabawi ﷺ (Qualities and Features of the Holy Prophet ﷺ)
lessons.notes_html:
What Khasail and Shamail Mean

  • Khasail and Shamail mean the excellent habits and characteristics of the Holy Prophet ﷺ.
  • They include his outward excellences, inward characteristics, day and night life (rising, sitting, eating, drinking, sleeping, waking), temperament, social life, dress, morals, behaviour with family and companions, outward appearance, Seerah, blessed features and physical build.
  • Khasail means habit; Shamail means good nature, excellent habit and virtuous quality.

Importance and Virtue

  • His pure life is the correct and complete picture of Islam; following his sayings, actions and blessed life is the means of salvation.
  • Allah says: For you there is an excellent model in the Messenger of Allah (Al-Ahzab: 21).
  • And: Indeed, your morals are exalted (Al-Qalam: 4).
  • He was the most courteous, most well-mannered, most truthful and generous, most righteous in deeds, most bound by promise and most trustworthy of all.

Helping Others

  • His way was sympathy and goodwill: Silah Rahmi, carrying the burdens of the helpless, helping the empty-handed, honouring the guest, and helping in calamities in the path of truth.
  • Listening to the cries of the oppressed and widows was his favourite occupation; he once postponed worship to recover a strangers loan from Abu Jahl.
  • He did good even to the enemy: at the Conquest of Makkah he forgave his nation and announced: Today there is no blame upon you; go, you are all free.

Household Life

  • Hazrat Aisha (RA) said he cleaned his clothes himself, milked the goat himself, did his own work and stitched his own clothes.
  • Hazrat Anas (RA) said he never saw anyone more kind and merciful to his family than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
  • He behaved cheerfully with family, fulfilled their needs, and greeted them with salaam on entering the house.

Lessons for Daily Life

  • Classroom: respect and gentleness with teacher and classmates. School: cleanliness and discipline.
  • Home: serving parents and helping in household work. Neighbourhood: care for neighbours needs and taking the lead in salaam.
  • Playground: honesty and cooperation. City: cleanliness and respecting the rights of others.
  • With neighbours: good conduct, gifts, visiting the sick, condoling, inviting one another, and helping the weak of society.

mcqs.q: By Khasail and Shamail of the Holy Prophet ﷺ is meant what?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is excellent habits and characteristics. Khasail means habit and Shamail means good nature, excellent habit and virtuous quality.

mcqs.q: Which verse calls the Messenger of Allah ﷺ an excellent model for believers?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Al-Ahzab: 21, Laqad kana lakum fi Rasulillahi uswatun hasanah — for you there is an excellent model in the Messenger of Allah.

mcqs.q: Which verse bears witness: Indeed, your morals are exalted?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Surah Al-Qalam: 4, Wa innaka la-ala khuluqin azeem — Indeed, your morals are exalted, as quoted in the lesson.

mcqs.q: When the Holy Prophet ﷺ went to the Jewish boy, what did he do?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is invited him to Islam. The book MCQ (C-2) states that when he went to the Jewish boy, he invited him to Islam.

mcqs.q: At the Conquest of Makkah, what did he do to the people of his nation?
options: Forced them to leave the city
mcqs.why: The correct answer is forgave them. Instead of revenge for years of oppression, he announced: Today there is no blame upon you; go, you are all free.

mcqs.q: According to Hazrat Aisha (RA), which household work did he do himself?
options: Cleaning and stitching his own clothes
mcqs.why: The correct answer is cleaning and stitching his own clothes. Hazrat Aisha (RA) said he cleaned his clothes, milked the goat, did his own work and stitched his clothes himself.

mcqs.q: Who said he never saw anyone more kind and merciful to his family than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Anas (RA). The lesson quotes Hazrat Anas (RA) that he never saw any person more kind and merciful to his family.

mcqs.q: What did he do on entering the house, according to the lesson?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is greeted family members with salaam. The lesson says he behaved cheerfully, fulfilled their needs, and greeted family with salaam upon entering.

mcqs.q: Which act is listed among his way of helping others, as Hazrat Khadijah (RA) described?
options: Silah Rahmi and carrying burdens of the helpless
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Silah Rahmi and carrying burdens of the helpless. His way was sympathy and goodwill: Silah Rahmi, helping the empty-handed and honouring the guest.

mcqs.q: For the neighbourhood, his blessed life teaches which behaviour?
options: Good conduct, gifts and visiting the sick
mcqs.why: The correct answer is good conduct, gifts and visiting the sick. It also teaches condoling, inviting one another, helping the weak, and doing good even to the enemy.

lessons.title: Manaqib-e-Ahl-e-Bait Athar (Virtues of the Ahl-e-Bait)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Manaqib and Ahl-e-Bayt

  • Manaqib is Arabic; its singular Manqabah means praise, goodness, excellence and virtue — the deeds and virtues of a famous personality, in prose or poetry.
  • Ahl-e-Bayt literally means household members: Ahl means members/people and Bayt means house.
  • In Quranic terminology, Ahl-e-Bayt is the household of the Holy Prophet ﷺ: his pure family (Aal-e-Pak), pure wives and children.

Hadith-e-Kisa and Love for Ahl-e-Bayt

  • Narrated from Hazrat Aisha Siddiqua (RA): he called Hazrat Fatimah-uz-Zahra, Hazrat Ali, Hazrat Hasan and Hazrat Husain (RA) under a cloak and prayed: O Allah, these are my Ahl-e-Bayt; remove impurity from them and purify them (Tirmidhi: 3871). This is also linked with Ayat-e-Tatheer.
  • Hadith-e-Thaqalayn: I leave two things with you; as long as you hold them firmly you will not go astray: the Book of Allah and my Ahl-e-Bayt (Tirmidhi: 3786).
  • About Hazrat Fatimah (RA): Fatimah is a part of my body; whoever angered her, angered me (Bukhari: 3093).
  • For Hasan and Husain (RA): These two are my sons; O Allah, I love them, You too love them, and love the one who loves them (Tirmidhi: 3775).
  • Scholars declared love and honour of Ahl-e-Bayt equal to love and honour of the Holy Prophet ﷺ.

Ummahat-ul-Mumineen

  • The Quran calls his pure wives Ummahat-ul-Mumineen, mothers of the believers: Wa azwajuhu ummahatuhum (Al-Ahzab: 6). Their number is eleven.
  • Hazrat Khadijah-ul-Kubra (RA): first wife, first to bring faith. Hazrat Aisha Siddiqua (RA): daughter of Abu Bakr Siddique, a great woman jurist.
  • Hazrat Zainab bint Khuzaimah (RA) was Umm-ul-Masakeen; Hazrat Zainab bint Jahsh (RA) is also among them.
  • The rest include Sawdah bint Zamah, Hafsah bint Umar, Umm-e-Salamah, Juwairiyah bint Al-Harith, Umm-e-Habibah (Ramlah bint Abu Sufyan), Safiyyah bint Huyayy, Maymunah bint Harith and Mariyah Qibtiyyah (RA).

Four Rights of Ahl-e-Bayt

  • They should be loved.
  • These respected persons should be obeyed.
  • Belief should be kept that they are just (Adil).
  • Those who love them should be loved, and those who hate them should be hated.

mcqs.q: The pure wives of the Holy Prophet ﷺ are called in the Quran what?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Ummahat-ul-Mumineen, mothers of the believers, from Wa azwajuhu ummahatuhum in Surah Al-Ahzab: 6.

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of Ahl-e-Bayt?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is household members. Ahl means members/people and Bayt means house, so Ahl-e-Bayt means the members of the household.

options: Manqabah — praise, goodness, excellence and virtue
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Manqabah meaning praise, goodness, excellence and virtue. In technical terms it means the deeds and virtues of a famous personality.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is Fatimah, Ali, Hasan and Husain (RA). He entered them under a cloak and prayed for their purification (Tirmidhi: 3871).

options: The Book of Allah and my Ahl-e-Bayt
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Book of Allah and my Ahl-e-Bayt. He said as long as you hold them firmly you will not go astray (Tirmidhi: 3786).

mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Fatimah (RA). The saying Fatimah is a part of my body is recorded in Sahih Al-Bukhari: 3093.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is eleven. The lesson states their number is eleven and lists them, from Khadijah-ul-Kubra to Mariyah Qibtiyyah (RA).

mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Khadijah-ul-Kubra (RA). The lesson calls her the first wife and the first to bring faith.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is they should be loved. The four rights are love, obedience, belief that they are just, and loving their lovers and hating their haters.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is Umm-ul-Masakeen. The lesson gives this title to Hazrat Zainab bint Khuzaimah (RA), while great woman jurist describes Hazrat Aisha (RA).

lessons.title: Manaqib-e-Sahaba Kiram and Ashra Mubashirah (Virtues of the Companions and the Ten Promised Paradise)
lessons.notes_html:
Who is a Sahabi?

  • Sahabi is derived from the Arabic word Suhbah, whose literal meaning is friendship.
  • In technical terms, a Sahabi is the personality who met the Holy Prophet ﷺ in the state of faith and died with the safety of faith.
  • From their Seerah we learn truthfulness, trustworthiness, sacrifice and obedience to the Messenger ﷺ, and keeping their love and respect in the heart.

Virtues of the Companions

  • Through the Companions, the Quran, Sunnah and the whole religion reached us; through their sacrifices Islam reached every corner of the world.
  • He said: The best era is that of my era (Bukhari: 3651); and: The best people among you are those of my era, then those after them, then those after them (Bukhari: 6695).
  • Glad tidings: Great glad tidings for the person who saw me and believed in me, and for the one who saw such a person who had seen me — glad tidings for the Companion and the Tabii.
  • Allah is pleased with the foremost Muhajireen and Ansar and those who followed them in goodness, and prepared gardens beneath which rivers flow; they will remain there forever — the great success (At-Tawbah: 100).
  • After the Prophets (AS), they hold the highest glory and exalted rank among all human beings on earth. Heartfelt love for them is exactly faith; even a little disrespect to them is a great sin.
  • He warned: Do not speak ill of my Companions; if one of you gave Mount Uhud in gold as charity, it would not reach even one Mudd of theirs (Bukhari: 3673, Muslim: 222).

Ashrah Mubashsharah

  • Ashrah means ten; Mubashsharah is from Basharah, meaning to give glad tidings. They are the ten human beings given glad tidings of Paradise in this world itself.
  • Their patience, justice and service to creation are lessons for daily life.
  • The ten names (Tirmidhi: 3747): Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique, Hazrat Umar Farooq, Hazrat Usman Ghani, Hazrat Ali Al-Murtaza, Hazrat Talhah, Hazrat Zubayr, Hazrat Abdur Rahman bin Awf, Hazrat Sad, Hazrat Saeed and Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah (RA).

mcqs.q: A Sahabi is one who, in the state of faith, did what with the Holy Prophet ﷺ?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is met him. A Sahabi met the Holy Prophet ﷺ in the state of faith and died with the safety of faith, as the lesson defines.

mcqs.q: From which Arabic word is Sahabi derived, and what does it mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Suhbah meaning friendship. The lesson states Sahabi is derived from Suhbah, whose literal meaning is friendship.

mcqs.q: In the hadith, which era is declared the best era?
options: The era of the Holy Prophet ﷺ
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the era of the Holy Prophet ﷺ. He said the best people are those of my era, then those after them, then those after them (Bukhari: 6695).

mcqs.q: What does Ashrah Mubashsharah mean?
options: Ten human beings given glad tidings
mcqs.why: The correct answer is ten human beings given glad tidings. They are the ten Companions given glad tidings of Paradise in this world itself.

mcqs.q: What does the word Ashrah literally mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is ten. In Arabic Ashrah means ten, while Mubashsharah is derived from Basharah, meaning to give glad tidings.

mcqs.q: According to Surah At-Tawbah: 100, with whom is Allah pleased?
options: The foremost Muhajireen and Ansar and their good followers
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the foremost Muhajireen and Ansar and those who followed them in goodness. Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him.

mcqs.q: What reward has Allah prepared for them in At-Tawbah: 100?
options: Gardens beneath which rivers flow, forever
mcqs.why: The correct answer is gardens beneath which rivers flow, forever. The verse calls remaining in them forever the great success.

mcqs.q: Charity equal to Mount Uhud in gold would still not reach what of a Companion?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is even one Mudd of theirs. He said do not speak ill of my Companions, for Uhud of gold would not reach even one Mudd of theirs (Bukhari: 3673).

mcqs.q: Through whom did the Quran, Sunnah and the whole religion reach us?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is through the Companions. The lesson states that through the Companions (RA) the Quran and Sunnah and the whole religion reached us.

mcqs.q: Which pair is correctly included in the Ashrah Mubashsharah list (Tirmidhi: 3747)?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Talhah and Hazrat Zubayr (RA). Both are named in the ten: Abu Bakr, Umar, Usman, Ali, Talhah, Zubayr, Abdur Rahman bin Awf, Sad, Saeed and Abu Ubaidah.

lessons.title: Importance and Excellence of Knowledge (Ilm)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Ilm

  • The literal meaning of Ilm is knowing and becoming aware.
  • The word Taleem is used for giving and teaching knowledge to others.
  • In technical terms, knowing the reality of a thing through man's five senses and intellect is called Ilm.

Why Knowledge Makes Man Honourable

  • The Lord of the universe made man the noblest of creation (Ashraf-ul-Makhlooqat) and blessed him with knowledge and intellect.
  • Through knowledge alone, the whole universe was made subservient for man.
  • Knowledge alone is the cause of man attaining honour over all other creation.
  • Knowledge is the basis of greatness and honour for man, and the means of exaltation.
  • It is an attribute of Allah Almighty: He is the Knower of the Unseen and the Knower of what is in the hearts; He alone grants to all creation the knowledge of its need.

Islam and the Value of Knowledge

  • At the time when Islam began in Arabia, the world was unaware of the importance of knowledge.
  • Islam revealed the value and worth of knowledge, and created in people the desire to acquire knowledge.
  • Surah Al-Mujadilah (11): Those among you who believed, and those who were given knowledge — Allah Almighty will raise their ranks. Here, in high ranks, knowledge has been mentioned along with faith.
  • Surah Taha (114): O my Sustainer! Increase me in knowledge.

Hadith on Knowledge and Scholars

  • إِنَّ الْعُلَمَاءَ وَرَثَةُ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ — The scholars alone are the heirs of the Prophets (AS). (Sunan Tirmidhi, Hadith: 2682)
  • One understanding scholar is heavier for Satan than a thousand worshippers. (Sunan Ibn Majah: 222)
  • طَلَبُ الْعِلْمِ فَرِيضَةٌ عَلَى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ — Seeking knowledge is obligatory upon every Muslim (man and woman). (Sunan Ibn Majah: 224)

The Holy Prophet (PBUH) as a Teacher

  • He taught with gentleness and ease.
  • He explained with examples.
  • He took care of the mental level of the students.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is knowing and becoming aware, because the lesson gives this as the literal meaning of Ilm, while giving and teaching knowledge is Taleem.

mcqs.q: In technical terms, Ilm is knowing the reality of a thing through what?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is man's five senses and intellect, because the lesson defines Ilm in technical terms as knowing the reality of a thing through them.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is the scholars, because the hadith says: The scholars alone are the heirs of the Prophets (Sunan Tirmidhi, Hadith: 2682).

options: It is optional for a few people
It is only for male students

It is obligatory upon every Muslim (man and woman)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that seeking knowledge is obligatory upon every Muslim, man and woman, as stated in Sunan Ibn Majah, Hadith: 224.

mcqs.q: Through what alone was the whole universe made subservient for man?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is knowledge, because the lesson says that through knowledge alone the whole universe was made subservient for man.

options: They will be given great wealth
Allah Almighty will raise their ranks

They will rule over all creation
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that Allah Almighty will raise their ranks, which is the translation given for Surah Al-Mujadilah, verse 11, in the lesson.

mcqs.q: Which dua for knowledge is taught in Surah Taha (114)?
options: O my Sustainer! Give me long life
O my Sustainer! Give me wealth
O my Sustainer! Increase me in knowledge
O my Sustainer! Make me powerful
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'O my Sustainer! Increase me in knowledge', which is the translation of Surah Taha, verse 114, given in the lesson.

mcqs.q: According to Sunan Ibn Majah (222), one understanding scholar is heavier for Satan than:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a thousand worshippers, because the hadith says one understanding scholar is heavier for Satan than a thousand worshippers.

mcqs.q: How did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) teach as a teacher?
options: With gentleness and ease, explaining with examples
Without giving any examples at all
Only to students of a high mental level
mcqs.why: The correct answer is teaching with gentleness and ease and explaining with examples, because the lesson lists these as his way of teaching.

mcqs.q: In Surah Al-Mujadilah (11), knowledge is mentioned, in high ranks, along with what?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is faith, because the lesson notes that in this verse knowledge has been mentioned along with faith in connection with high ranks.

lessons.title: Importance of Family in Islam
lessons.notes_html:
What is a Family?

  • Khandan (family) is a Persian word whose literal meaning is household, family, tribe, children and lineage.
  • The collection of close relatives of the same generation is the concept of family life.
  • The important members of the family — mother, father, wife, husband and children — hold basic status.
  • Social life begins with the family and household. The family begins with the mutual Nikah of a man and a woman (husband and wife).
  • Apart from man, the concept of family and relations does not exist in any other creation.

Family in Islam

  • Islam gives equal importance to man and woman; each one's sphere is fixed.
  • Islam exhorts and emphasises the fulfilment of the rights and duties of each one.
  • Surah Al-Hujurat (13): O mankind! Indeed, We created you from one man and one woman.
  • Man behaves at home with respect and honour, love and affection, in the capacity of mother, father, grandparents, siblings and children.
  • The objectives of family life are the survival of the human race and its increase, peace and contentment through married life, and mutual love and affection between husband and wife. Through Nikah, the chain of the human race continues with survival, and with human greatness and honour.

Rights and Duties of Husband and Wife

  • وَلَهُنَّ مِثْلُ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوْفِ (Al-Baqarah: 228) — The rights of women upon men are the same as, according to custom, the rights of men upon women.
  • The husband must provide food and drink, expenses, clothing, house, treatment and other needs according to his financial means.
  • The husband must allow the wife to keep mahr, given money or other personal property, and to do business within permissible limits.
  • The husband must behave with love and affection, not oppress or wrong the family, adopt justice and kindness, and fulfil their rights according to Shariah.
  • The wife must, in the husband's absence, protect wealth, property and her honour like a trust, and not allow any non-mahram to enter the house without the husband's permission. (An-Nisa: 34)
  • The wife should not demand expenses more than the husband's income and financial status; in hardship she should show overlooking and endurance instead of complaining to others unnecessarily.
  • The wife should not reveal the secrets of the husband or the house, should protect the lineage, and take better care and training of the children, and serve and obey the husband.
  • خَيْرُكُمْ خَيْرُكُمْ لِأَهْلِهِ وَأَنَا خَيْرُكُمْ لِأَهْلِي — The best among you is the one who is best for his family, and I am the best among you for my family. (Sunan Ibn Majah, Hadith 2052)

Respect for Parents

  • Among all relations, the relation of parents is important and worthy of respect; it is because of them that we came into this world.
  • Surah Al-Isra (23-24): Worship none besides Allah, and do good to parents. If one or both reach old age, do not even say 'Uff' to them, do not scold them, speak with great respect, lower your neck in humility with kindness, and say: O my Sustainer! Have mercy on them, as they raised me with mercy when I was small.
  • The rights of parents upon children are: honour and respect, obedience and submission, good conduct, good conduct with the near ones and companions of parents, confession of gratitude, and dua for forgiveness.

Rights of Children

  • Give children the training of the necessary matters of religion, the education of the Holy Quran, and Salah.
  • Teach children Islamic values, and deal with equality and justice among children in inheritance.
  • Include daughters also, like sons, in gifts and love; do not become sad at the birth of a daughter, because expressing displeasure is ingratitude.
  • Avoid every kind of harshness and violence against children, and keep a behaviour of kindness and love and affection with them.
  • Do not kill one's children because of hunger and poverty.
  • The charm of the family is children, and having children is a great blessing of Allah Almighty.
  • Those relatives with whom Nikah cannot take place are called Mahram.

Acts That Harm the Family

  • Misuse of mobile and internet, disobedience to parents, household quarrels, distrust in relations, wasteful spending, and giving preference to outside friends over home.

mcqs.q: With what does a family begin in Islam?
options: With the birth of the first child
With the mutual Nikah of a man and a woman
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the mutual Nikah of a man and a woman, because the lesson says the family begins with the Nikah of husband and wife.

mcqs.q: What does Surah Al-Hujurat (13) say about the creation of mankind?
options: Mankind was created in separate unrelated groups
We created you from one man and one woman
Mankind was created only for worship of wealth
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that Allah created mankind from one man and one woman, as translated from Surah Al-Hujurat, verse 13, in the lesson.

options: The husband, according to his financial means
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the husband according to his financial means, because the lesson lists providing these needs as the husband's responsibility.

mcqs.q: What must a wife protect like a trust in her husband's absence?
options: Wealth and property, and her honour
Only the furniture of the house
mcqs.why: The correct answer is wealth and property and her honour, because the lesson says she protects them like a trust in the husband's absence.

mcqs.q: According to Surah Al-Isra (23-24), what must a child not even say to aged parents?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Uff', because the verse commands not even to say Uff to parents, not to scold them, and to speak with great respect.

options: To be treated with harshness and violence
To be excluded from gifts if a daughter
Equality and justice among children in inheritance
To be left without religious training
mcqs.why: The correct answer is equality and justice among children in inheritance, which the lesson lists among the rights of children.

mcqs.q: According to the hadith (Sunan Ibn Majah: 2052), the best among you is the one who:
options: Is best for his friends only
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the one who is best for his family, because the Prophet (PBUH) said this and added that he was the best for his own family.

mcqs.q: The beauty (charm) of the family is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is children, because the lesson states that the charm of the family is children and having children is a great blessing of Allah.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is Mahram, because the lesson defines Mahram as those relatives with whom Nikah cannot take place.

options: Demand expenses more than the husband's income and financial status
Protect the secrets of the house
mcqs.why: The correct answer is demanding expenses beyond the husband's income, because the lesson says she should not demand more than his income and financial status.

lessons.title: Respect for Humanity (Ehtram-e-Insaniyat)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Respect for Humanity

  • Ihtiram means honour and value, virtue and superiority.
  • Ihtiram-e-Insaniyat means the honour and greatness of man.
  • Man is the best creation of Allah Almighty on earth; he has superiority over all creation.
  • Every human being has the rank and status of honour and virtue.
  • Protecting the life, wealth and honour of every human being — whatever his colour, race, religion, language, nation and country — on behalf of his humanity is called Ihtiram-e-Insaniyat.

The Quran on Human Honour

  • وَلَقَدْ كَرَّمْنَا بَنِيْ آدَمَ (Surah Al-Isra: 70) — We have granted honour to the children of Adam.
  • إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَتْقَاكُمْ (Al-Hujurat: 13) — Indeed, the most honourable among you in the sight of Allah Almighty is the one who is most pious.
  • Allah Almighty has granted man great honour and dignity (Surah Al-Isra: 70).
  • Islam declared the distinction of colour, race, language and homeland invalid; the standard of greatness and nobility is only Taqwa and the fear of Allah Almighty.
  • The Holy Quran made man the caliph and deputy on earth, informed him of everything, and freed him from the slavery of all his objects of worship.
  • In all these blessed verses, generally, only man has been given status, whether Muslim or non-Muslim.

Before Islam and the Teaching of Islam

  • The era before Islam is called the Age of Ignorance, in which respect for humanity had almost ended.
  • Islam, rejecting false ideas and customs, taught human beings the lesson of respect for humanity, and declared qualities like arrogance and self-liking as bad.
  • The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said: O mankind! You are all the children of one father; therefore, any person considering himself greater than others and being arrogant is a matter of foolishness and ignorance. (Musnad Ahmad, Hadith: 23489)

Acts Against Respect for Humanity

  • Being arrogant; considering oneself worthy of pride before Allah Almighty or creation, in intellectual, scholarly, financial or lineage terms.
  • Considering people inferior, making fun of them, adopting a mocking behaviour, and making accusations.
  • Oppression, excess or injustice with people; finding faults in them and trying to spy.
  • Taunting a person because of a physical or practical shortcoming, calling him by bad nicknames, or dishonouring him in any way.
  • Treating children unequally on the basis of young and old, wise and unwise, or son and daughter.
  • Talking with immorality, foul language or in a bad manner. Examples of respect in daily life are helping a poor person and respecting elders.

options: Honour and value, virtue and superiority
mcqs.why: The correct answer is honour and value, virtue and superiority, because the lesson gives exactly this meaning for the word Ihtiram.

mcqs.q: Protecting the life, wealth and honour of every human being, whatever his colour, race, religion, language, nation and country, is called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Ihtiram-e-Insaniyat, because the lesson defines respect for humanity as protecting every person's life, wealth and honour.

mcqs.q: What does Surah Al-Isra (70) declare about the children of Adam?
options: We have granted honour to the children of Adam
They are honoured only by wealth
Only some nations were granted honour
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that Allah granted honour to the children of Adam, which is the translation of Surah Al-Isra, verse 70, in the lesson.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is the most pious person, because the verse says the most honourable in Allah's sight is the one who is most pious (most Taqwa).

mcqs.q: What station did the Holy Quran give to man on earth?
options: Slave of his objects of worship
Owner of all other creation by force
mcqs.why: The correct answer is caliph and deputy on earth, because the lesson says the Quran made man Allah's caliph and deputy on earth.

mcqs.q: In the Age of Ignorance before Islam, respect for humanity had:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it had almost ended, because the lesson describes the pre-Islamic Age of Ignorance in exactly these words.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an act AGAINST respect for humanity?
options: Taunting a person and calling him by bad nicknames
mcqs.why: The correct answer is taunting and bad nicknames, because the lesson lists taunting a person for a shortcoming and calling by bad nicknames among acts against respect.

mcqs.q: Which distinctions did Islam declare invalid as a standard of greatness?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is colour, race, language and homeland, because Islam declared these distinctions invalid and made Taqwa the only standard of greatness.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is children of one father, because the Prophet (PBUH) said all mankind are children of one father, so arrogance is foolishness and ignorance.

options: Only if he belongs to one nation
Only if he is a scholar
mcqs.why: The correct answer is whether Muslim or non-Muslim, because the lesson says these verses give status to man generally, Muslim or non-Muslim.

lessons.title: Collective Justice (Ijtimai Adl)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Adl

  • Adl is an Arabic word whose literal meaning is: to straighten, to equalise, to compare between two things, and to adopt moderation between two conditions.
  • In technical terms, the concept of Adl is very vast: placing a thing in its correct place — fully abiding by truth in word and deed, dealing with every person without any favour or concession, and giving him what he deserves.
  • Against Adl comes Zulm (oppression), that is, placing a thing out of place.
  • Adl with an oppressor is that he should be prevented from oppressing.

Quranic Guidance on Collective Justice

  • Surah An-Nahl (90): Indeed, Allah Almighty commands justice, goodness, and giving to relatives, and forbids immodesty, evil talk and oppression. He advises you so that you may understand.
  • The purpose of this verse is that all human beings should live with justice and fairness in their collective life, and end oppression and excess, so that their social life becomes a centre of peace and tranquillity.
  • Surah An-Nisa (58): When you judge between people, judge with justice. Indeed, Allah Almighty advises you a very good thing. Surely Allah Almighty is All-Hearing.
  • For the one who judges, both parties should be equal — whether friend or enemy, one's own or a stranger, Muslim or non-Muslim, near or far, rich or poor.
  • اِعْدِلُوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ (Al-Ma'idah: 8) — Do justice, because it is closer to Taqwa.
  • If justice and fairness are established in the country, society will become peaceful and tranquil.

Evils of Ignoring Collective Justice

  • By ignoring justice, restlessness and corruption are created in society; the first cause of corruption is deviating from Adl.
  • Corruption is created in society when its members abandon Adl.
  • By not establishing justice in the economy, society does not become prosperous, and some member of society remains deprived of basic needs.
  • Without establishing equality in all spheres of life, man's life cannot become better, because special balance and moderation in all spheres of life is necessary.

Measures to Establish Collective Justice

  • Legal equality: all are equal in the eyes of the law, and the law should apply to all without exception — whether rich or poor, officer or subordinate, friend or enemy.
  • Collective justice in economic matters: every person should be free to adopt a lawful means of livelihood according to his abilities and choice, and lawful means of earning a livelihood should not be closed for any person.
  • Collective justice in judicial matters: Islam has presented a regular system of justice, which is called Qaza or judiciary.
  • Establishment of a just society: all human beings are equal as human beings; no one has superiority because of belonging to a class, family, nation or region.

lessons.title: Iffat and Haya (Chastity and Modesty)
lessons.notes_html:
Concepts of Iffat, Ismat and Haya

  • Iffat is an Arabic word whose literal meaning is piety and purity. Its Shariah concept is: remaining chaste, adopting moral purity, keeping the desires of the self under control, and protecting the self from a bad path and from acts like adultery and immodesty.
  • Along with Iffat comes the word Ismat, whose meaning is chastity, innocence and nobility.
  • The literal meaning of Haya is shame and self-respect (Ghairat). Haya is a natural and moral quality placed inside man, by which, due to the fear of God, he saves himself from immodesty and immorality and tries to stay away from evil; such a person is called modest (Haya-dar).

Importance of Iffat and Haya

  • Iffat and Haya hold the status of soul and life in the list of Islamic morals.
  • Allah Almighty taught the Muslims Iffat and Haya, and gave this great quality the highest place among all Islamic virtues.
  • Iffat and Haya are the basis of man's nobility, honour and chastity.
  • When man destroys his Haya, he becomes like a wild beast and runs after his desires.

Virtue in the Quran and Hadith

  • وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حَافِظُونَ (Al-Mu'minoon: 5) — And (the successful believer is) the one who protects his private parts.
  • Every religion has some morals, and the morals of Islam is Haya. (Muwatta Imam Malik, Hadith: 2634)
  • Indeed, Allah Almighty is Modest and Concealing, and He likes modesty and concealment. (Sunan Abi Dawood, Hadith: 4012)
  • وَالْحَيَاءُ شُعْبَةٌ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ — Haya is a great branch of faith. (Bukhari: 9, Muslim: 30)
  • Narrated from Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA): Faith has more than seventy branches, among which Haya is also a great branch. (Bukhari: 9, Muslim: 30)
  • Narrated from Hazrat Umar (RA): Faith and Haya have a deep connection with each other. When one goes, the other also goes. (Al-Adab-ul-Mufrad by Al-Bukhari: 1313)
  • Some wise men stated the ranks of Haya to be three: 1. Following the commands of God and avoiding forbidden things, 2. Staying away from harming people, 3. Being modest with oneself in solitude, considering Allah present in every condition and avoiding sins.

The Haya of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)

  • Narrated from Hazrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA): The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was the most Iffat- and Haya-possessing of all.
  • He (PBUH) was more modest than even a virgin veiled woman, and if he saw something disliked, its effect used to appear on his blessed face. He had a natural hatred for evil things. (Sunan Abi Dawood, Hadith: 4797)

Manifestations of Iffat and Haya

  • Iffat and Haya relate not only to character and action, but also to thought and thinking, speech and manner. Every Muslim man and woman should give priority to them, to be counted a respectable, useful citizen and a person preparing for the Hereafter.
  • Conversation: It is not appropriate for a believer to talk with abuse, foul language and in an unpleasant manner; rather he should adopt good talk or silence.
  • Dress: Islam has stated two purposes of dress — covering (Satr) and adornment (Zeenat). Men and women should adopt dress in which both purposes are attained, keeping in view Haya and veil.
  • Sitting and rising: A true believer should avoid immodesty and indecent activities at all times in his daily routines. The Holy Quran commands believing men and women to keep their gazes lowered and protect their Iffat and Ismat.
  • Gathering: In time spent among people in a gathering, meeting or consultative activity, Iffat and Haya should remain in sitting, rising, conversation and manner.

lessons.notes_html:
Lineage and Family

  • His full name is Husain bin Ali bin Abi Talib bin Abdul Muttalib bin Hashim.
  • His father is Sher-e-Khuda Hazrat Ali (may Allah honour his face).
  • His mother is Khatoon-e-Jannat Hazrat Fatimah-uz-Zahra (RA), the daughter of Hazrat Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (PBUH).
  • From both the mother's and father's sides, he is Hashmi, a possessor of honour and virtue.

Virtues in the Ahadith of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)

  • The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said: "Fatimah is the leader of the women of Paradise, and Hasan and Husain are the leaders of the youth of Paradise." (Sunan Tirmidhi: 3781)
  • The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said: "Whoever loves Hasan and Husain, indeed he loves me; and whoever hates them, indeed he hates me."
  • Loving Hazrat Hasan and Husain (RA) is equal to loving the Messenger of Allah (PBUH), and hating both of them is equal to hating the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
  • Once in a street of Madinah Munawwarah, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) saw Hazrat Imam Husain (RA) playing with children; he caught him smiling, kissed his forehead, and said: "Husain is from me, and I am from Husain. May Allah Almighty love the one who loved Husain. Husain is a grandson among grandsons." (Sunan Ibn Majah, Hadith: 144)
  • The Messenger of Allah (PBUH) said: "I granted my awe and leadership to Hasan, and I granted my courage and generosity to Husain." (Al-Mu'jam Al-Kabeer by At-Tabarani: 18508)

Character — Correcting a Person's Wudu

  • From childhood, he was a possessor of high Seerah and morals in intelligence and wisdom.
  • Once he went to the mosque with his brother Sayyiduna Imam Hasan (RA) and saw a person doing Wudu incorrectly.
  • He said: "O uncle! We both are doing Wudu; see whether we are making any mistake in Wudu."
  • When both Imams did Wudu correctly, the man realised his own Wudu was not correct.
  • In this way, he corrected his Wudu without embarrassing that person. (Bihar-ul-Anwar, Imam Majlisi 43, p. 319)

Refusal of Yazid's Bay'at and the Tragedy of Karbala

  • After Yazid sat on the throne, Imam Husain (RA) was called to pledge Bay'at to Yazid, but he refused and set out for Makkah Mukarramah.
  • He stayed in Makkah Mukarramah for four months.
  • The people of Kufa sent letters asking him to come to Kufa so they may pledge Bay'at at his hand, because besides him they have no leader and Imam, and in the Yazidi government Islamic traditions are being trampled.
  • He sent his cousin Muslim bin Aqeel (RA) to Kufa to assess the conditions there.
  • Yazid removed the governor of Kufa, Hazrat Nu'man bin Bashir (RA), and appointed Ubaidullah bin Ziyad as governor, ordering him to imprison or kill Muslim bin Aqeel (RA).
  • Muslim bin Aqeel had informed Imam Husain (RA) that the people of Kufa had pledged Bay'at, but Ibn Ziyad had Muslim bin Aqeel martyred.
  • Imam Husain (RA), with his family, set out from Makkah Mukarramah for Kufa on 8 Dhu-ul-Hijjah 60 Hijri.
  • After a very difficult journey of forty-four days, he reached the plain of Karbala on 2 Muharram-ul-Haram 61 Hijri.
  • The commander of the Yazidi army, Umar bin Sa'd, insisted from 2 Muharram-ul-Haram to 10 Muharram-ul-Haram that he pledge Bay'at to Yazid, but he clearly refused to bow before falsehood.
  • On 10 Muharram-ul-Haram 61 Hijri, in the battle of truth and falsehood, he was martyred one by one along with his family and devoted ones.
  • Today Karbala is a famous city of Iraq, where his blessed shrine is located and that is his resting place.

lessons.notes_html:
Family Introduction

  • He is known in Islamic history by his Kuniyyat (teknonym) Abu Ubaidah.
  • His real name is Aamir bin Abdullah bin Al-Jarrah bin Hilal.
  • He belonged to the Banu Fahr branch of the Quraysh.
  • His mother was from the Banu Harith tribe, who had accepted Islam.
  • His father was killed in the Battle of Badr in the state of disbelief.

Birth and Attribution to His Grandfather

  • His family was originally a resident of Makkah.
  • He was born in the house of Abdullah bin Al-Jarrah Al-Fahri, eleven years after Aam-ul-Feel, and he grew up in Makkah itself.
  • Because his father was killed in the Battle of Badr in the state of disbelief, due to Islamic honour he did not like to include the name of his non-Muslim father with his name.
  • Attributing himself to his grandfather, he began to be called Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah.

Why He Is Called Ameen-e-Hadhihi-ul-Ummah

  • In the ninth year of Hijrah, some People of the Book from the region of Najran in Yemen came to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) for a scholarly debate.
  • After failing, they finally agreed to pay Jizyah and requested: "O Messenger of Allah (PBUH)! You fix Jizyah upon us; we will pay it, and send a trustworthy person with us."
  • Then the Holy Prophet (PBUH), holding the hand of Hazrat Abu Ubaidah, said: "This person is the Ameen (trustworthy) of this Ummah." (Sahih Bukhari, Hadith 4380)
  • Therefore, he is called "Ameen-e-Hadhihi-ul-Ummah".

Sariyyah Saif-ul-Bahr — Special Help

  • The Holy Prophet (PBUH) sent an army of three hundred Companions under the leadership of Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah (RA) towards the seashore (Saif-ul-Bahr).
  • On the way, their food ran out, so they began to survive by eating leaves of trees.
  • Then, with the special help of Allah Almighty, a huge fish (Al-Anbar) came onto the shore from the sea, eating which they survived for a month.
  • On return, its meat was presented in the service of the Holy Prophet (PBUH); he ate it and said that this is sustenance given by Allah.

Simple Life, Contentment and Zuhd

  • He used to eat very simple food and wear simple clothes.
  • He got the position of leading the Islamic army and handling the governorship of Syria, but these things had no effect on his contentment and asceticism (Zuhd).
  • In the time of Hazrat Umar Farooq (RA), when he was commander of the army on the expedition of Syria and Palestine, Hazrat Umar (RA) came to his tent and saw no valuable goods except a sword and a shield, and there was no bedding either.
  • Hazrat Umar (RA) said: "O Abu Ubaidah! Keep some goods of necessity with you."
  • He replied: "O Ameer-ul-Mu'mineen! This very condition of ours will very soon take us to our resting place, that is, Paradise." (Musannaf Abdur Razzaq, Kitab-ul-Jami', Bab Zuhd-us-Sahabah 11/311)

Migrations and Passing Away

  • He first migrated towards Abyssinia, and then towards Madinah Munawwarah, attaining the honour of both migrations.
  • In those days, the military camp of the Muslims was in Amwas, in the nearby region of Palestine, when the disease of plague (Ta'oon) began to spread.
  • He passed away in 18 Hijri at the age of 59 years due to the plague of Ta'oon.

lessons.notes_html:
Family, Birth and Names

  • His full name is Jabir bin Hayyan bin Abdullah Al-Kufi.
  • His title is "Sufi" and his Kuniyyat is "Abu Musa"; Europeans know him by the name "Geber".
  • His forefathers belonged to Tus in Khurasan, where he was born in the tribe of Azd in 102 Hijri.
  • Because of these relations, he used to write, along with his name in his books, "Kufi", "Azdi", "Tusi" or "Sufi".
  • His grandfather's name was Abdullah.

His Father's Business

  • The father of Jabir, Hayyan bin Abdullah, used to do the business of Attar (perfume).
  • On coming to Tus, he opened a "perfume shop" through his ancestral art.

Services in the Science of Chemistry — Founder of Chemistry

  • He is remembered in the science of chemistry with the title of "Founder of Chemistry".
  • He was the first chemist who divided matter into three parts: plants, animals and minerals.
  • He then divided minerals into three parts: things that turn into vapours, things that melt on fire, and those things which do not melt on heating.
  • Through different ingredients and chemical processes, he prepared a substance which dissolved everything; its name became "acid" (for example: sulphuric acid, hydrochloric acid).
  • Through his efforts, the foundation of a new scientific art, "chemistry", was laid.
  • He invented an apparatus named "Qar' Anbiq" for extracting essence (Arq) by heating herbs and fruits, which in today's age is called "Qarnfal" (retort).
  • Many of his Arabic books were translated into Latin, and then into English, and reached Europe; thus, because of him, Europe became acquainted with the science of chemistry.

Famous Inventions

  • Acids (sulphuric acid, hydrochloric acid).
  • The apparatus named "Qar' Anbiq" (which is called "Qarnfal" today) for extracting essence from herbs and fruits.
  • "Carbonate arsenic sulphide", "the method of making dye (Khizab)", "calcining metals", and "methods of polishing iron".
  • Apart from this, he also invented new things in pharmacy and metallurgy, which were not known to anyone before.

Writings

  • He is counted among the prolific writers.
  • The number of his treatises and books is more than 232.
  • According to one saying, his writings are more than five hundred, most of which were lost, having fallen victim to the conditions of the age.
  • Many of his Arabic books were translated into Latin, and then from Latin into English, and reached Europe.
  • His other books are about astronomy, physics, geometry, philosophy and logic, and political science.
  • His books related to the science of chemistry are: "Izah", "Al-Khawas Al-Kabeer" and "Al-Mizan". (A'zam Ulama, Kimiya Jabir bin Hayyan, p. 20)

lessons.notes_html:
Family Lineage

  • His full name is Syed Muhammad Rashid bin Muhammad bin Baqa bin Muhammad Imam Shah.
  • His title is "Rozi Dhani" and his Kuniyyat is "Abu Yaseen".
  • He is the forefather of the Rashidi family of the famous Syed tribe of Sindh.
  • His chain of lineage, after the fourth generation, meets Hazrat Imam Husain, son of Ameer-ul-Mu'mineen Hazrat Ali (may Allah honour his face).
  • The forefather of his family is Hazrat Syed Ali Makki (RA), who left his homeland for the propagation of the religion of Islam and adopted residence near the ancient city of Sindh, Sewistan (Sehwan), in Lak Ari; for this reason, his family became famous as Lakiyari.

Birth and the Title Rozi Dhani

  • His birth took place in Ramadan-ul-Mubarak 1171 Hijri, in a village Raheem Dino Kalhoro, near Khairpur Mirs.
  • In Ramadan-ul-Mubarak, his habit of drinking milk was such that at the time of Sehri, drinking his mother's milk, he used to spend the whole day like fasting people, and at the Maghrib Azan, he used to cling to his mother again for milk.
  • Because of this habit, he used to be called "Rozi Dhani" (one who keeps fasts); later, attributing him to his shrine (Roza), he was called "Rozi Dhani".

Early Education

  • His father, Hazrat Syed Muhammad Baqa (RA), had fixed a special time for the training of his children and started giving early education at home itself to his sons, including Syed Muhammad Rashid (RA).
  • After that, he kept getting education from Hafiz Zainuddin Mahesar (RA) and Mian Muhammad Akram Ghamro (RA).
  • Then, for further education, he was seated in the Maktab of the famous elder of Shikarpur, Shah Faqirullah Alvi (RA).
  • After that, his father admitted him in the Madrasah of the famous scholar of Kotri Muhammad Kabir, in the present district of Naushahro Feroze, Makhdum Yar Muhammad Siddiqui (RA).
  • After getting education from there, he was sent to the Ustad-ul-Kul of Arija village, near Larkana, Hazrat Maulana Muhammad Arijvi (RA), from whom he obtained the certificate of completion (Faraghat).

Scholarly Services and Writings

  • He was not only perfect in spiritual knowledge, but he had complete command over outward sciences, especially Tafsir, Hadith, Fiqh, Tasawwuf, history, lexicography, and sciences and arts.
  • He had an extraordinary attachment to the Persian and Arabic languages.
  • Some book or the other used to be in his hand all the time, and he also had a large scholarly library.
  • To create a love for books among people, he used to say: "Whoever buys expensive books, knowledge will never leave his children."
  • His famous writings are: Jami-ul-Jawami', Persian dictionary (in four large volumes), "Aadab-ul-Mureedeen", "Maktoobat", "Sharh Asma Allah-ul-Husna" and "Jami' Sindhi Kalam".

Spiritual Services

  • He used to keep inviting the common people towards guidance and the religion.
  • He obtained the initial training of Sulook from his respected father, Hazrat Muhammad Baqa Shah (RA), in the Naqshbandi order, and then in the Qadri way.
  • At the age of twenty-seven, he was appointed the successor of his respected father.
  • Along with his scholarly benefit, his spiritual benefit also proved beneficial for the hearts of thousands of people.
  • After obtaining Khilafat in Sulook from his respected father, he travelled, besides Sindh, to Punjab, and the regions of India: Kutch, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Kathiawar and Balochistan, and kept giving scholarly and spiritual benefit to people.
  • He also played a mujahid-like role to end the wrong customs and innovations spread in society.
  • The collection of his sermons and advice, sayings and conditions, "Malfoozat Sharif", is famous by the name of Pir Muhammad Rashid Rozi Dhani (RA), which his Khalifas compiled.
